```{r fig-priors, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8.2, fig.cap = "Figure 5. Prior densities on the square-root scale: (a) regression coefficients; (b) the scale σ of the t innovations η_t; (c) the AR(1) coefficient; (d) the degrees of freedom ν."}
# Prior densities for the sqrt(kWh) model. Values match the model-code chunk (Section 4):
#   intercept N(0, 20^2), other coefficients N(0, 5^2), sigma ~ half-t(3, scale 2),
#   phi uniform on the stationary region, nu - 2 ~ Exponential(mean 10).
# The innovations are eta_t ~ t_nu(0, sigma); missing days are left out of the likelihood,
# so neither latent weights nor missing days need a prior.
# Uses from earlier chunks: d (full calendar, date as Date)

TAU_INT <- 20   # intercept prior SD          (PRIOR_TAU$sqrt[1] in the model code)
TAU_OTH <- 5    # other coefficients prior SD (PRIOR_TAU$sqrt[2])
A_SIGMA <- 2    # half-t scale for sigma      (PRIOR_SIGMA_A$sqrt)

col_nav <- "#1f4e79"; col_teal <- "#148f77"; col_red <- "#b03a2e"; col_gold <- "#b9770e"

# reference values from the observed days only, used to show the priors are wide
sq_p  <- sqrt(d$kwh)                                   # NA on missing days (dropped by na.rm)
mon_p <- format(d$date, "%m")
mon_means <- tapply(sq_p, mon_p, mean, na.rm = TRUE)   # 12 monthly means of sqrt(kWh)
hi_m  <- names(which.max(mon_means))
lo_m  <- names(which.min(mon_means))
gap_p <- max(mon_means) - min(mon_means)               # largest gap between monthly means
sd_p  <- sd(sq_p, na.rm = TRUE)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 3.2, 1.2))

# (a) regression coefficients
xb <- seq(-50, 50, length.out = 800)
d_int <- dnorm(xb, 0, TAU_INT)
d_oth <- dnorm(xb, 0, TAU_OTH)
plot(xb, d_oth, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = col_teal, ylim = c(0, 1.1 * max(d_oth)),
     xlab = "coefficient (sqrt kWh)", ylab = "prior density", main = "(a) Regression coefficients")
lines(xb, d_int, lwd = 2, col = col_nav)
arrows(-gap_p / 2, 0.006, gap_p / 2, 0.006, code = 3, length = 0.05, lwd = 2, col = col_red)
text(gap_p / 2 + 1, 0.012,
     sprintf("%s-%s gap, %.1f sqrt kWh", month.abb[as.integer(lo_m)], month.abb[as.integer(hi_m)], gap_p),
     col = col_red, cex = 0.75, adj = 0)
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c(col_nav, col_teal), cex = 0.75,
       legend = c(sprintf("intercept, SD %g", TAU_INT), sprintf("other coefficients, SD %g", TAU_OTH)))

# (b) scale of the t innovations: folded t_3 with scale A, f(s) = 2 * dt(s/A, 3) / A for s > 0
xs <- seq(0.01, 10, length.out = 600)
ds <- 2 * dt(xs / A_SIGMA, df = 3) / A_SIGMA
plot(xs, ds, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = col_nav,
     xlab = expression("scale" ~ sigma ~ "of the innovations (sqrt kWh)"), ylab = "prior density",
     main = expression("(b) Innovation scale" ~ sigma))
abline(v = sd_p, lty = 2, lwd = 1.5, col = col_red)
text(sd_p + 0.2, 0.9 * max(ds), sprintf("SD of daily sqrt kWh = %.2f", sd_p), col = col_red, cex = 0.75, adj = 0)
text(6.5, 0.5 * max(ds), sprintf("half-t, 3 df\nscale %g", A_SIGMA), col = col_nav, cex = 0.75)

# (c) AR(1) coefficient: uniform on the stationary interval
plot(NA, xlim = c(-1.45, 1.45), ylim = c(0, 0.75), xaxt = "n",
     xlab = expression("autoregressive coefficient" ~ phi), ylab = "prior density",
     main = "(c) AR(1) coefficient")
rect(-1.45, 0, -1, 0.75, col = "#f6e6e4", border = NA)
rect(1, 0, 1.45, 0.75, col = "#f6e6e4", border = NA)
rect(-1, 0, 1, 0.5, col = adjustcolor(col_nav, 0.18), border = col_nav, lwd = 2)
text(0, 0.58, "stationary: shocks fade", col = col_nav, cex = 0.75)
text(-1.22, 0.62, "excluded", col = col_red, cex = 0.65, srt = 90)
text(1.22, 0.62, "excluded", col = col_red, cex = 0.65, srt = 90)
axis(1, at = c(-1, 0, 1))

# (d) degrees of freedom of the t innovations: nu - 2 ~ Exp(mean 10)
nu_grid <- seq(2.02, 48, length.out = 500)
dn <- dexp(nu_grid - 2, rate = 0.1)
plot(nu_grid, dn, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = col_nav,
     xlab = expression("degrees of freedom" ~ nu), ylab = "prior density", main = "(d) Tail weight")
abline(v = 2, lty = 2, lwd = 1.5, col = col_red)
abline(v = 12, lty = 3, lwd = 1.5, col = col_gold)
text(3.1, 0.085, expression(nu == 2), col = col_red, cex = 0.75, adj = 0)
text(13.2, 0.07, "prior mean of nu = 12", col = col_gold, cex = 0.75, adj = 0)
text(32, 0.04, "nearly\nGaussian", col = col_nav, cex = 0.75)
```
This dataset was previously been used mainly to benchmark machine-learning forecasters at minute or hourly resolution (e.g., Kim & Cho, 2019), including Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty estimation (Zaman et al., 2022). We instead fit an interpretable Bayesian regression to daily totals, with seasonal, weekly, autoregressive and heavy-tailed components. There are no published estimates of these model parameters for a comparable household, so we utilized weakly informative priors to allow our data to be the primary thing informing our posterior distributions (Table 6, Figure 5). 

The priors are centered at zero and are not derived from the data; we compare them with summaries of the data only to confirm that they are wide relative to plausible values. With our large sample size (over 1,000 training days), we expect posterior estimates to be insensitive to this choice, but the tail parameter $\nu$, which the data inform least, may not be. Therefore, Section 6 refits the model with the coefficient prior standard deviations halved and doubled, and with the prior on $\nu$ shifted toward heavier and toward lighter tails.

First, the intercept $\beta_0$ has a normal prior, which is continuous, symmetric, and allows any real value. Its standard deviation of 20 $\sqrt{\text{kWh}}$ places 95% of the prior within ±40 $\sqrt{\text{kWh}}$ (up to 40² = 1,600 kWh/day), far above the current average for a Sceaux household (about 9.6 kWh per day; GridLabs, n.d.), this household’s highest observed day (about 80 kWh), and even the physical maximum of a residential connection (864 kWh/day; EDF, Tarif Bleu), so the prior does not constrain the intercept. Our mean is 0 not because we believe the baseline level is zero, but because with that standard deviation, it is nonrestrictive (Figure 5a).  

Second, our other regression coefficients $\beta_1, a_j, b_j, \delta_k$ also have normal priors centered at 0 for similar reasons: it is continuous, symmetric, lets the data choose the direction of each effect, and makes extremely large effects less plausible. Their standard deviation of 5 √kWh is about twice the largest contrast in the data (Figure 5a).

Third, the innovation scale $\sigma$ has a half-$t$ prior with 3 degrees of freedom and scale 2 √kWh (Gelman, 2006), which we sample through its inverse-gamma mixture form (Huang & Wand, 2013)

It keeps $\sigma$ positive and its heavy tails allows scales well above the standard deviation of daily √kWh, 1.01 (Figure 5b). 

Fourth, the autoregressive coefficients have a uniform prior on the stationary region: $(-1, 1)$ for AR(1), and the corresponding stationary region for the higher-order models compared in Section 5. Within that region every value is equally likely, and shocks fade over time, so long-horizon forecasts stay bounded (Figure 5c).

Fifth, for our degrees of freedom $\nu$, we choose an exponential prior with mean 10 for $\nu-2$, for similar reasons of why we chose the half-t distribution. We want to restrict the values to values greater than 2 (the t distribution only has finite variance when the degrees of freedom are greater than 2), and we're trying to accommodate heavy-tailed innovations [(the exponential distribution allows us to do this while also assigning less probability to extremely large values. The degrees of freedom determine how heavy the innovation distribution's tails are: smaller values produce heavier tails, while larger values produce increasingly Gaussian-like distributions. The Exponential prior allows us to accommodate heavy-tailed innovations by assigning substantial prior density to values of $\nu$ near 2, while progressively reducing the density assigned to extremely large values of $\nu$. **Shorter alternative of this paragraph:** Fifth, an exponential prior with mean 10 on $\nu - 2$ keeps $\nu$ above 2, so the innovation variance is finite. It puts substantial weight on small values (heavy tails) and less on very large ones (nearly Gaussian tails), so the data decide how heavy the tails are (Figure 5d).

#! prior for latent weights ???

Together, these choices regularize the parameters without imposing a direction or size on the household's demand patterns in advance.

# 4. Posterior Computation and Diagnostics

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(\beta, \phi, \sigma, \nu \mid z_O) \;\propto\;
& \underbrace{\prod_{t \in \mathcal{I}_p}
\frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{\nu+1}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{\nu}{2}\right)\sigma\sqrt{\nu\pi}}
\left(1 + \frac{\eta_t^2}{\nu\sigma^2}\right)^{-\frac{\nu+1}{2}}}_{\text{likelihood}} \\[6pt]
&\times \underbrace{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,20}\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_0^2}{2\cdot 20^2}\right)}_{\beta_0 \,\sim\, N(0,\,20^2)}
\;\underbrace{\prod_{\theta \in \{\beta_1,\, a_j,\, b_j,\, \delta_k\}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,5}\exp\left(-\frac{\theta^2}{2\cdot 5^2}\right)}_{\text{each } \sim\, N(0,\,5^2)} \\[6pt]
&\times \underbrace{\frac{2}{\pi\sqrt{3}}\left(1 + \frac{\sigma^2}{3 \cdot 2^2}\right)^{-2}\mathbb{1}\{\sigma > 0\}}_{\sigma \,\sim\, \text{half-}t_3(0,\,2)}
\;\times\; \underbrace{\frac{\mathbb{1}\{\phi \in \mathcal{S}_p\}}{\text{vol}(\mathcal{S}_p)}}_{\phi \,\sim\, \text{Uniform}(\mathcal{S}_p)}
\;\times\; \underbrace{\frac{1}{10}\exp\left(-\frac{\nu-2}{10}\right)\mathbb{1}\{\nu > 2\}}_{\nu - 2 \,\sim\, \text{Exp}(\text{mean } 10)}
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\eta_t = (z_t - x_t^{T}\beta) - \sum_{l=1}^{p}\phi_l(z_{t-l} - x_{t-l}^{T}\beta)$, $\mathcal{I}_p$ is the set of days observed together with their previous $p$ days, and $\mathcal{S}_p$ is the stationary region of the AR($p$) coefficients ($\mathcal{S}_1 = (-1, 1)$, so for AR(1) the prior density is $\tfrac12\mathbb{1}\{|\phi| < 1\}$).  

OR A MORE COMPACT VERSION WITHOUT THE CONSTANTS:
$$
p(\beta, \phi, \sigma, \nu \mid z_O) \;\propto\;
\prod_{t \in \mathcal{I}_p} \frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{\nu+1}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{\nu}{2}\right)\sigma\sqrt{\nu}}
\left(1 + \frac{\eta_t^2}{\nu\sigma^2}\right)^{-\frac{\nu+1}{2}}
\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_0^2}{800} - \frac{\beta_1^2 + \sum_j (a_j^2 + b_j^2) + \sum_k \delta_k^2}{50}\right)
\left(1 + \frac{\sigma^2}{12}\right)^{-2}
e^{-(\nu-2)/10},
$$
for $\sigma > 0$, $\phi \in \mathcal{S}_p$ and $\nu > 2$, and zero otherwise.

```{r model-code, echo = FALSE}
# Bayesian harmonic regression with AR(p) errors and Student-t innovations.
#
# MODEL
#   Response on a chosen scale: z_t = g(y_t), with g = sqrt, or identity.
#   Defined on the daily calendar t = 1, ..., T; missing days stay NA.
#
#       z_t   = x_t' beta + eps_t
#       eps_t = sum_{l=1}^{p} phi_l eps_{t-l} + eta_t
#       eta_t ~ t_nu(0, sigma)          (scale sigma; heavy = FALSE gives N(0, sigma^2))
#
#   x_t contains: intercept, centered linear trend in years, J harmonic pairs at
#   period 365 days, and six day-of-week dummies (Monday is the baseline).
#
# LIKELIHOOD (conditional; missing days left out under MAR)
#   A day enters the likelihood only if it and its p previous days are observed,
#   so each run of observed days is conditioned on its first p days
#   (Box et al., 2015). No latent weights, no imputation.
#
# PRIORS
#   beta    ~ N(0, diag(tau^2)), tau set by response scale (weakly informative)
#   sigma   ~ half-t(3, 0, A)
#   phi     ~ Uniform over the stationary region
#   nu - 2  ~ Exponential(mean 10)
#
# SAMPLING
#   One block random-walk Metropolis on theta = (beta, log sigma, phi, log(nu - 2)).
#   log sigma and log(nu - 2) are unconstrained (with Jacobian terms in the log
#   posterior); phi proposals outside the stationary region are rejected.
#   Proposal covariance = c * Sigma, Sigma = inverse Hessian of -log posterior at
#   its mode (Laplace); c is tuned during burn-in toward ~23% acceptance, then frozen.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# set priors
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
PRIOR_TAU <- list(identity = c(100.0, 40.0), sqrt = c(20.0, 5.0)) # SD for the intercept, SD for all other coeffs
PRIOR_SIGMA_A <- list(identity = 20.0, sqrt = 2.0)                 # the half-t scale for sigma

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# moving between scales (response scale)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
to_model_scale <- function(y, scale) {
  switch(scale, sqrt = sqrt(y), identity = y, stop("unknown scale: ", scale))
}

from_model_scale <- function(z, scale) {
  # On the sqrt scale the model puts negligible mass below zero; such draws map to 0 kWh.
  switch(scale, sqrt = pmax(z, 0)^2, identity = z, stop("unknown scale: ", scale))
}

log_jacobian <- function(z, scale) {
  # log |dz/dy|, which turns a density for z into a density for daily kWh.
  switch(scale, sqrt = -log(2) - log(z), identity = 0 * z, stop("unknown scale: ", scale))
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build the design matrix (n x 12)
# intercept, centered trend, 2 harmonics, 6 day-of-week dummies
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_design <- function(t, dow, J, t_center = NULL) {
  # t: 1-based integer day index. dow: 0 = Monday. Returns list(X, names).
  t <- as.numeric(t)
  if (is.null(t_center)) t_center <- mean(t)
  cols <- list(rep(1, length(t)), (t - t_center) / 365.0)
  xnames <- c("intercept", "trend_per_year")
  if (J >= 1) {
    for (j in seq_len(J)) {
      cols[[length(cols) + 1]] <- sin(2 * pi * j * t / 365.0)
      cols[[length(cols) + 1]] <- cos(2 * pi * j * t / 365.0)
      xnames <- c(xnames, paste0("sin_h", j), paste0("cos_h", j))
    }
  }
  daynames <- c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
  for (k in 1:6) {
    cols[[length(cols) + 1]] <- as.numeric(as.integer(dow) == k)
    xnames <- c(xnames, paste0("dow_", daynames[k + 1]))
  }
  list(X = do.call(cbind, cols), names = xnames)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AR(p) helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
is_stationary <- function(phi) { # TRUE if phi is inside the stationary region (the uniform prior's support)
  # Roots of 1 - phi_1 B - ... - phi_p B^p outside the unit circle.
  p <- length(phi)
  if (p == 0) return(TRUE)
  companion <- matrix(0, p, p)
  companion[1, ] <- phi
  if (p > 1) companion[2:p, 1:(p - 1)] <- diag(p - 1)
  max(Mod(eigen(companion, symmetric = FALSE, only.values = TRUE)$values)) < 1 - 1e-8
}

stationary_cov <- function(phi, sigma2) { # cov(first p errors) under stationarity; used by the validation simulation
  p <- length(phi)
  if (p == 0) return(matrix(numeric(0), 0, 0))
  if (p == 1) return(matrix(sigma2 / (1 - phi[1]^2), 1, 1))
  A <- matrix(0, p, p)
  A[1, ] <- phi
  if (p > 1) A[2:p, 1:(p - 1)] <- diag(p - 1)
  Q <- matrix(0, p, p)
  Q[1, 1] <- sigma2
  M <- diag(p * p) - kronecker(A, A)                 # vec(V) = (I - A kron A)^{-1} vec(Q)
  V <- matrix(solve(M, as.vector(Q)), p, p)
  0.5 * (V + t(V))
}

log_t <- function(e, sigma, nu, heavy) { # log density of a scaled t (or normal) distribution
  # sigma and nu may be scalars or vectors recycling against e.
  if (!isTRUE(heavy) || !all(is.finite(nu))) {
    return(-0.5 * log(2 * pi) - log(sigma) - 0.5 * (e / sigma)^2)
  }
  lgamma(0.5 * (nu + 1)) - lgamma(0.5 * nu) - 0.5 * log(pi * nu) - log(sigma) -
    0.5 * (nu + 1) * log1p((e / sigma)^2 / nu)
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# sampler: one block random-walk Metropolis
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
fit <- function(
  y, observed, t, dow, J = 2, p = 1, heavy = TRUE, scale = "sqrt",
  n_iter = 20000, burn = 5000, thin = 5, seed = 1, ll_index = NULL,
  n_paths = 400, disperse_init = FALSE, verbose = FALSE,
  prior_tau = PRIOR_TAU[[scale]], prior_sigma_A = PRIOR_SIGMA_A[[scale]],
  nu_exp_mean = 10.0) {
  # Run one chain. y and observed are on the full daily grid (length T);
  # y may contain NA wherever observed is FALSE (those days are left out).
  # ll_index: days at which the pointwise log-likelihood is recorded for WAIC
  #   (pass the same set to every model); NULL = this model's own likelihood days.
  # disperse_init: start from an overdispersed draw around the mode, so chains with
  #   different seeds start apart and split-Rhat can detect non-convergence.
  # prior_tau, prior_sigma_A, nu_exp_mean: priors of Report section 3; override for
  #   sensitivity analyses. Returns posterior draws (rows = saved iterations).
  set.seed(seed)
  y <- as.numeric(y)
  observed <- as.logical(observed)
  nT <- length(y)
  des <- build_design(t, dow, J)
  X <- des$X
  xnames <- des$names
  k <- ncol(X)
  z <- rep(NA_real_, nT)
  z[observed] <- to_model_scale(y[observed], scale)   # missing days stay NA
  miss_idx <- which(!observed)

  # days in the likelihood: observed, with their p previous days observed
  idx <- common_ll_index(observed, max_lag = p)
  ll_idx <- if (is.null(ll_index)) idx else as.integer(ll_index)

  # ---- parameter vector theta = (beta, log sigma, phi, log(nu - 2)) ----
  i_b <- seq_len(k)
  i_s <- k + 1L
  i_p <- if (p > 0) k + 1L + seq_len(p) else integer(0)
  i_n <- if (heavy) k + p + 2L else integer(0)
  d_th <- k + 1L + p + as.integer(heavy)
  unpack <- function(th) list(beta = th[i_b], sigma = exp(th[i_s]), phi = th[i_p],
                              nu = if (heavy) 2 + exp(th[i_n]) else Inf)
  prior_sd <- c(prior_tau[1], rep(prior_tau[2], k - 1))
  nu_sigma <- 3   # half-t degrees of freedom for sigma

  # innovations eta_t = eps_t - sum_l phi_l eps_{t-l} on a set of days
  innov <- function(r, ph, days) {
    e <- r[days]
    for (l in seq_len(p)) e <- e - ph[l] * r[days - l]
    e
  }

  log_post <- function(th) {
    q <- unpack(th)
    if (p > 0 && !is_stationary(q$phi)) return(-Inf)               # phi: uniform on the stationary region
    r <- z - as.numeric(X %*% q$beta)                               # eps_t (NA on missing days)
    ll <- sum(log_t(innov(r, q$phi, idx), q$sigma, q$nu, heavy))    # conditional t log-likelihood
    lp_beta  <- -0.5 * sum((q$beta / prior_sd)^2)                   # normal priors on beta
    lp_sigma <- -0.5 * (nu_sigma + 1) * log1p(q$sigma^2 / (nu_sigma * prior_sigma_A^2)) +
                th[i_s]                                             # half-t prior + Jacobian of log sigma
    lp_nu    <- if (heavy) -(q$nu - 2) / nu_exp_mean + th[i_n] else 0   # Exp prior + Jacobian of log(nu - 2)
    ll + lp_beta + lp_sigma + lp_nu
  }

  # ---- mode and Laplace covariance for the proposal ----
  b0 <- qr.solve(X[observed, , drop = FALSE], z[observed])           # least squares on observed days
  r0 <- z - as.numeric(X %*% b0)
  th0 <- c(b0, log(sd(r0, na.rm = TRUE)), rep(0.3 / max(p, 1), p), if (heavy) log(6))
  neg <- function(th) { v <- log_post(th); if (is.finite(v)) -v else 1e10 }
  mode <- optim(th0, neg, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 2000, reltol = 1e-10))$par
  H <- optimHess(mode, neg)
  eg <- eigen((H + t(H)) / 2, symmetric = TRUE)
  Sigma <- eg$vectors %*% diag(1 / pmax(eg$values, 1e-8), d_th) %*% t(eg$vectors)  # kept positive definite
  L <- t(chol(Sigma))
  step <- 2.38 / sqrt(d_th)                                           # scale on the SD scale: c = step^2

  # ---- starting value ----
  th <- mode
  if (disperse_init) {
    for (try in 1:1000) {
      cand <- mode + 2 * as.numeric(L %*% rnorm(d_th))                # overdispersed: 2 x the Laplace SD
      if (is.finite(log_post(cand))) { th <- cand; break }
    }
  }
  lp <- log_post(th)

  # ---- output storage (same structure as before) ----
  n_keep <- length(seq(from = burn, to = n_iter - 1L, by = thin))
  out <- list(
    beta = matrix(0, n_keep, k), sigma = numeric(n_keep), phi = matrix(0, n_keep, p),
    nu = numeric(n_keep), eps_last = matrix(0, n_keep, max(p, 1L)),
    loglik = matrix(0, n_keep, length(ll_idx)), ll_idx = ll_idx, names = xnames
  )
  warm_names <- c("sigma", "nu", if (p > 0) paste0("phi_", seq_len(p)), xnames)
  n_warm <- length(seq(from = 0L, to = burn - 1L, by = thin))
  out$warmup <- matrix(NA_real_, n_warm, length(warm_names), dimnames = list(NULL, warm_names))
  path_every <- max(1L, n_keep %/% max(as.integer(n_paths), 1L))
  path_slots <- length(seq(from = 0L, to = n_keep - 1L, by = path_every))
  out$eps_path <- matrix(NA_real_, path_slots, nT)
  out$wt_path <- matrix(NA_real_, path_slots, nT)  # weight the t likelihood implies per day: (nu+1)/(nu+(eta/sigma)^2)
  out$path_pars <- matrix(0, path_slots, 3L + p)
  sv <- 0L; psv <- 0L; wv <- 0L
  acc_win <- 0; acc_post <- 0; n_post <- 0L

  for (it in 0:(n_iter - 1L)) {
    # ---- one block proposal for all parameters ----
    prop <- th + step * as.numeric(L %*% rnorm(d_th))
    lp_prop <- log_post(prop)
    took <- is.finite(lp_prop) && log(runif(1)) < lp_prop - lp
    if (took) { th <- prop; lp <- lp_prop }

    # ---- tune the step size during burn-in, then freeze it ----
    if (it < burn) {
      acc_win <- acc_win + took
      if ((it + 1L) %% 200L == 0L) {
        step <- min(max(step * exp(acc_win / 200 - 0.234), 0.01), 5)
        acc_win <- 0
      }
    } else {
      acc_post <- acc_post + took
      n_post <- n_post + 1L
    }

    # ---- save ----
    if (it >= burn && (it - burn) %% thin == 0L && sv < n_keep) {
      q <- unpack(th)
      r <- z - as.numeric(X %*% q$beta)
      sv <- sv + 1L
      out$beta[sv, ] <- q$beta
      out$sigma[sv] <- q$sigma
      out$nu[sv] <- q$nu
      if (p > 0) {
        out$phi[sv, ] <- q$phi
        out$eps_last[sv, seq_len(p)] <- rev(r[(nT - p + 1L):nT])
      }
      out$loglik[sv, ] <- log_t(innov(r, q$phi, ll_idx), q$sigma, q$nu, heavy) + log_jacobian(z[ll_idx], scale)
      if ((sv - 1L) %% path_every == 0L && psv < path_slots) {
        psv <- psv + 1L
        out$eps_path[psv, ] <- r
        e_t <- innov(r, q$phi, idx)
        out$wt_path[psv, idx] <- if (heavy) (q$nu + 1) / (q$nu + (e_t / q$sigma)^2) else 1
        out$path_pars[psv, 1] <- q$sigma
        out$path_pars[psv, 2] <- q$nu
        if (p > 0) out$path_pars[psv, 4:(3L + p)] <- q$phi
      }
    }
    if (it < burn && it %% thin == 0L) {
      q <- unpack(th)
      wv <- wv + 1L
      out$warmup[wv, ] <- c(q$sigma, q$nu, q$phi, q$beta)
    }
    if (verbose && (it + 1L) %% 5000L == 0L) {
      q <- unpack(th)
      message(sprintf("    iter %d/%d  sigma=%.3f phi=%s nu=%.1f  step=%.2f",
                      it + 1L, n_iter, q$sigma, paste(round(q$phi, 3), collapse = " "), q$nu, step))
    }
  }

  out$acc_rate <- c(block = acc_post / max(n_post, 1L))   # acceptance after burn-in (step frozen)
  out$miss_idx <- miss_idx
  out$X <- X
  out$scale <- scale
  out$J <- J
  out$p <- p
  out$heavy <- heavy
  out$prop_cov <- step^2 * Sigma
  out
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# multi-chain driver
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
stack_along_chains <- function(xs) {
  x1 <- xs[[1]]
  d <- dim(x1)
  nC <- length(xs)
  if (is.null(d)) {
    out <- matrix(0, nC, length(x1))
    for (i in seq_len(nC)) out[i, ] <- xs[[i]]
    return(out)
  }
  out <- array(0, c(nC, d[1], d[2]))
  if (d[2] == 0) return(out)
  for (i in seq_len(nC)) out[i, , ] <- xs[[i]]
  out
}

fit_chains <- function(y, observed, t, dow, n_chains = 4, seed = 1, ...) {
  chains <- lapply(seq_len(n_chains) - 1L, function(ch) {
    fit(y, observed, t, dow, seed = seed + 100 * ch, ...)
  })
  merged <- list()
  for (key in c("beta", "sigma", "phi", "nu", "eps_last", "loglik", "warmup", "acc_rate")) {
    merged[[key]] <- stack_along_chains(lapply(chains, `[[`, key))
  }
  for (key in c("eps_path", "wt_path", "path_pars")) {
    merged[[key]] <- do.call(rbind, lapply(chains, `[[`, key))
  }
  for (key in c("names", "ll_idx", "miss_idx", "X", "scale", "J", "p", "heavy")) {
    merged[[key]] <- chains[[1]][[key]]
  }
  merged
}

common_ll_index <- function(observed, max_lag = 2) {
  # Days that are observed and whose max_lag preceding days are also observed.
  # Indices are 1-based.
  observed <- as.logical(observed)
  nT <- length(observed)
  if (max_lag <= 0) return(which(observed))
  idx <- seq.int(max_lag + 1L, nT)
  keep <- vapply(idx, function(i) {
    observed[i] && all(observed[(i - max_lag):(i - 1L)])
  }, logical(1))
  idx[keep]
}

one_step_diagnostics <- function(merged, z_obs = NULL, observed) {
  # From the saved error paths, compute per-day one-step-ahead standardised
  # residuals and posterior predictive p-values under the fitted model.
  # Returns a list of length-T vectors (NA on days that are not evaluable).
  eps <- merged$eps_path
  pars <- merged$path_pars
  sigma <- pars[, 1]
  nu <- pars[, 2]
  p <- merged$p
  nT <- ncol(eps)
  S <- nrow(eps)
  phi <- if (p > 0) pars[, 4:(3L + p), drop = FALSE] else matrix(0, S, 0)

  pred <- matrix(0, S, nT)
  if (p > 0) {
    for (k in seq_len(p)) {
      pred[, (k + 1L):nT] <- pred[, (k + 1L):nT] + phi[, k] * eps[, seq_len(nT - k)]
    }
  }
  e <- eps - pred
  std <- e / sigma

  if (isTRUE(merged$heavy)) {
    cdf <- std
    cdf[] <- pt(as.numeric(std), df = rep(nu, times = nT))
  } else {
    cdf <- std
    cdf[] <- pnorm(as.numeric(std))
  }

  ok <- as.logical(observed)
  if (p > 0) {
    obs <- as.logical(observed)
    for (k in seq_len(p)) {
      ok[(k + 1L):nT] <- ok[(k + 1L):nT] & obs[seq_len(nT - k)]
    }
    ok[seq_len(p)] <- FALSE
  }

  list(
    std_resid_mean = ifelse(ok, colMeans(std), NA_real_),
    std_resid_sd = ifelse(ok, apply(std, 2, sd), NA_real_),
    ppp = ifelse(ok, colMeans(cdf), NA_real_),
    wt_mean = ifelse(ok, colMeans(merged$wt_path), NA_real_),   # posterior mean of the implied t weight
    # lam_mean = ifelse(ok, colMeans(merged$wt_path), NA_real_),  # posterior mean of the implied t weight
    evaluable = ok
  )
}

flatten <- function(merged, key) {
  # Collapse the (chain, draw, ...) axes into one. An empty trailing dimension
  # (p = 0 leaves phi empty) becomes a matrix with zero columns.
  a <- merged[[key]]
  d <- dim(a)
  if (length(d) == 2) {
    as.vector(t(a))
  } else if (length(d) == 3) {
    nC <- d[1]
    nD <- d[2]
    k <- d[3]
    if (k == 0) return(matrix(0, nC * nD, 0))
    out <- matrix(0, nC * nD, k)
    r <- 1L
    for (ch in seq_len(nC)) {
      sl <- array(a[ch, , , drop = FALSE], c(nD, k))
      out[r:(r + nD - 1L), ] <- sl
      r <- r + nD
    }
    out
  } else {
    stop("flatten() expected a matrix or a 3-way array")
  }
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# convergence diagnostics (rank-normalised split-Rhat and bulk ESS)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
rank_normalise <- function(x) {
  out <- x
  flat <- as.numeric(x)
  out[] <- qnorm((rank(flat, ties.method = "first") - 0.375) / (length(flat) + 0.25))
  out
}

split_rhat <- function(draws) {
  # draws: matrix with chains in rows and iterations in columns.
  n <- ncol(draws)
  half <- n %/% 2
  s <- rbind(draws[, seq_len(half), drop = FALSE], draws[, (half + 1L):(2L * half), drop = FALSE])
  n2 <- ncol(s)
  means <- rowMeans(s)
  W <- mean(apply(s, 1, var))
  B <- n2 * var(means)
  if (!is.finite(W) || W <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  var_hat <- ((n2 - 1) * W + B) / n2
  sqrt(var_hat / W)
}

ess <- function(draws) {
  # Bulk effective sample size via Geyer's initial positive sequence.
  m <- nrow(draws)
  n <- ncol(draws)
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(draws), rep(draws[1], length(draws)), tolerance = 1e-5))) {
    return(as.numeric(m * n))
  }
  acov <- matrix(0, m, n)
  for (ch in seq_len(m)) {
    x <- draws[ch, ] - mean(draws[ch, ])
    f <- fft(c(x, rep(0, n)))
    ac <- Re(fft(f * Conj(f), inverse = TRUE)) / (2 * n)
    acov[ch, ] <- ac[seq_len(n)] / n
  }
  chain_mean <- rowMeans(draws)
  mean_var <- mean(acov[, 1]) * n / (n - 1)
  var_plus <- mean_var * (n - 1) / n + (if (m > 1) var(chain_mean) else 0)
  rho_hat_even <- 1
  rho_hat_odd <- 1 - (mean_var - mean(acov[, 2])) / var_plus
  tau <- rho_hat_even + 2 * rho_hat_odd
  kk <- 1
  while (kk + 2 < n - 2 && (rho_hat_even + rho_hat_odd) > 0) {
    rho_hat_even <- 1 - (mean_var - mean(acov[, kk + 2])) / var_plus
    rho_hat_odd <- 1 - (mean_var - mean(acov[, kk + 3])) / var_plus
    if (rho_hat_even + rho_hat_odd > 0) tau <- tau + 2 * (rho_hat_even + rho_hat_odd)
    kk <- kk + 2
  }
  tau <- max(tau, 1 / log10(max(m * n, 11)))
  (m * n) / tau
}

diagnose <- function(draws) {
  # draws: matrix chain x iteration. Rank-normalised split-Rhat and bulk ESS,
  # plus the folded split-Rhat and the tail ESS at the 5% and 95% quantiles (Vehtari et al., 2021).
  rn <- rank_normalise(draws)
  q <- quantile(draws, c(0.05, 0.95))
  list(
    rhat = split_rhat(rn),
    rhat_folded = split_rhat(rank_normalise(abs(draws - median(draws)))),
    ess = ess(rn),
    ess_tail = min(ess((draws <= q[1]) * 1), ess((draws >= q[2]) * 1))
  )
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WAIC
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
waic <- function(loglik) {
  # loglik: array chain x draw x n_obs of pointwise log densities.
  d <- dim(loglik)
  nC <- d[1]
  nD <- d[2]
  n <- d[3]
  ll <- matrix(0, nC * nD, n)
  r <- 1L
  for (ch in seq_len(nC)) {
    ll[r:(r + nD - 1L), ] <- array(loglik[ch, , , drop = FALSE], c(nD, n))
    r <- r + nD
  }
  m <- apply(ll, 2, max)
  lppd_i <- log(colMeans(exp(sweep(ll, 2, m, "-")))) + m
  pwaic_i <- apply(ll, 2, var)
  elpd_i <- lppd_i - pwaic_i
  list(
    elpd_waic = sum(elpd_i),
    p_waic = sum(pwaic_i),
    waic = -2 * sum(elpd_i),
    se = sqrt(n * var(elpd_i)),
    n = n,
    elpd_i = elpd_i
  )
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# forecasting
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
forecast <- function(
  merged, t_future, dow_future, t_center, eps_init = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL, draw_idx = NULL, seed = 7
) {
  # Simulate the posterior predictive distribution of y on future days.
  # eps_init, if given, is (N, p) with columns (eps_origin, eps_origin-1, ...),
  # overriding the error state saved at the end of the fitted series (rolling origins).
  # Returns y (N, H) predictive draws (kWh), mu (N, H) systematic part (kWh),
  # loc (N, H) conditional mean on the modelling scale, plus sigma, nu, scale.
  set.seed(seed)
  beta <- flatten(merged, "beta")
  sigma <- flatten(merged, "sigma")
  phi <- flatten(merged, "phi")
  nu <- flatten(merged, "nu")
  eps_last <- flatten(merged, "eps_last")
  if (is.null(dim(beta))) beta <- matrix(beta, nrow = 1)
  if (is.null(dim(phi))) phi <- matrix(phi, nrow = length(sigma))
  if (is.null(dim(eps_last))) eps_last <- matrix(eps_last, nrow = length(sigma))
  N <- nrow(beta)
  if (!is.null(draw_idx)) {
    sel <- as.integer(draw_idx)
  } else if (!is.null(n_draws) && n_draws < N) {
    sel <- sample.int(N, n_draws)
  } else {
    sel <- seq_len(N)
  }
  if (length(sel) != N) {
    beta <- beta[sel, , drop = FALSE]
    sigma <- sigma[sel]
    phi <- phi[sel, , drop = FALSE]
    nu <- nu[sel]
    eps_last <- eps_last[sel, , drop = FALSE]
    N <- length(sel)
  }
  if (!is.null(eps_init) && nrow(as.matrix(eps_init)) != N) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "eps_init has %d rows but %d draws are in use; build it from the same draw_idx passed here.",
      nrow(as.matrix(eps_init)), N
    ))
  }

  p <- merged$p
  Xf <- build_design(t_future, dow_future, merged$J, t_center = t_center)$X
  H <- length(t_future)
  mu <- beta %*% t(Xf)
  hist <- if (p > 0) {
    if (is.null(eps_init)) eps_last[, seq_len(p), drop = FALSE] else as.matrix(eps_init)
  } else {
    matrix(0, N, 1)
  }

  z <- matrix(0, N, H)
  loc <- matrix(0, N, H)
  heavy <- merged$heavy
  for (h in seq_len(H)) {
    pred_eps <- if (p > 0) rowSums(phi * hist) else rep(0, N)
    loc[, h] <- mu[, h] + pred_eps
    eta <- if (heavy) sigma * rt(N, df = nu) else sigma * rnorm(N)   # t_nu(0, sigma) innovation
    e_new <- pred_eps + eta
    if (p > 0) {
      hist <- if (p == 1) cbind(e_new) else cbind(e_new, hist[, seq_len(p - 1L), drop = FALSE])
    }
    z[, h] <- mu[, h] + e_new
  }

  out <- list(sigma = sigma, nu = nu, scale = merged$scale, loc = loc, heavy = heavy, sel = sel)
  out$y <- from_model_scale(z, merged$scale)
  out$mu <- from_model_scale(mu, merged$scale)
  out
}

log_pred_density <- function(fc, y_actual) {
  # Exact-mixture log predictive density of the observed kWh values (final innovation
  # integrated analytically: t_nu or normal given the draw). Returns a vector of length H.
  y_actual <- as.numeric(y_actual)
  H <- ncol(fc$loc)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, H)
  z_act <- to_model_scale(y_actual, fc$scale)
  for (h in seq_len(H)) {
    if (!is.finite(z_act[h])) next
    ll <- log_t(z_act[h] - fc$loc[, h], fc$sigma, fc$nu, fc$heavy) + log_jacobian(z_act[h], fc$scale)
    m <- max(ll)
    out[h] <- m + log(mean(exp(ll - m)))
  }
  out
}

pit <- function(fc, y_actual) {
  # Probability integral transform from the predictive mixture (uniform if calibrated).
  y_actual <- as.numeric(y_actual)
  z_act <- to_model_scale(y_actual, fc$scale)
  H <- ncol(fc$loc)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, H)
  for (h in seq_len(H)) {
    if (!is.finite(z_act[h])) next
    s <- (z_act[h] - fc$loc[, h]) / fc$sigma
    out[h] <- if (isTRUE(fc$heavy)) mean(pt(s, df = fc$nu)) else mean(pnorm(s))
  }
  out
}

crps <- function(samples, y_actual) {
  # Exact CRPS of an ensemble forecast, one value per column of samples (N, H).
  y_actual <- as.numeric(y_actual)
  N <- nrow(samples)
  H <- ncol(samples)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, H)
  i <- 0:(N - 1L)
  for (h in seq_len(H)) {
    if (!is.finite(y_actual[h])) next
    x <- sort(samples[, h])
    term1 <- mean(abs(x - y_actual[h]))
    term2 <- 2 * sum((2 * i - N + 1) * x) / (N * N)
    out[h] <- term1 - 0.5 * term2
  }
  out
}
```

```{r validate-sampler, include = FALSE}
# ---- Sampler validation on simulated data ----
# Simulates a series from the model itself with known parameter values (sqrt scale, J = 2,
# AR(1) errors, Student-t innovations eta_t ~ t_nu(0, sigma)), blanks out the same 23 days
# that are missing in the real data, fits it with the block random-walk Metropolis sampler
# (missing days left out of the likelihood, as in the real analysis), and checks that the
# 95% credible intervals cover the true values.
# Uses from earlier chunks: d, here(), and the model-code functions
#   (build_design, stationary_cov, fit_chains, diagnose).
# Reruns when results/02_sampler_validation.rds is missing or was made by the old sampler.

val_file <- here("results", "02_sampler_validation.rds")

simulate_val <- function(d, J = 2, p = 1, seed = 0) {
  set.seed(seed)
  des <- build_design(d$t, d$dow, J)
  X <- des$X
  # true values close to the fitted sqrt(kWh) model
  beta_true <- c(5.00, -0.02, 0.42, 0.73, 0.10, -0.15,     # intercept, trend, sin1, cos1, sin2, cos2
                 0.05,  0.08, -0.05, 0.03, 0.40,  0.35)    # Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun
  stopifnot(length(beta_true) == ncol(X))
  phi_true <- rep(0.47, p)
  sigma_true <- 0.58
  nu_true <- 8.0

  Tlen <- nrow(d)
  eps <- numeric(Tlen)
  V0 <- stationary_cov(phi_true, sigma_true^2)              # start the simulated errors in the stationary state
  eps[seq_len(p)] <- as.numeric(t(chol(V0)) %*% rnorm(p))
  eta <- sigma_true * rt(Tlen, df = nu_true)                 # t_nu(0, sigma) innovations
  for (i in (p + 1):Tlen) eps[i] <- sum(phi_true * eps[(i - 1):(i - p)]) + eta[i]
  z <- as.numeric(X %*% beta_true + eps)
  y <- pmax(z, 0)^2                                          # back to kWh
  y[!d$observed] <- NA                                       # same missing days as the real data
  list(y = y, observed = d$observed, t = d$t, dow = d$dow, names = des$names,
       beta = beta_true, phi = phi_true, sigma = sigma_true, nu = nu_true, J = J, p = p)
}

validate_sampler <- function() {
  sim <- simulate_val(d)
  fitres <- fit_chains(sim$y, sim$observed, sim$t, sim$dow,
                       J = sim$J, p = sim$p, heavy = TRUE, scale = "sqrt",
                       n_iter = 40000, burn = 10000, thin = 5, n_chains = 4, seed = 11)
  one_row <- function(label, truth, draws2d) {
    flat <- as.numeric(draws2d)
    qs <- quantile(flat, c(0.025, 0.975))
    dg <- diagnose(draws2d)
    data.frame(Parameter = label, Truth = truth, `Posterior mean` = mean(flat),
               `2.5%` = qs[[1]], `97.5%` = qs[[2]], Covered = qs[[1]] <= truth && truth <= qs[[2]],
               `R-hat` = dg$rhat, ESS = dg$ess, check.names = FALSE)
  }
  rows <- c(lapply(seq_along(sim$names), function(i) one_row(sim$names[i], sim$beta[i], fitres$beta[, , i])),
            list(one_row("sigma", sim$sigma, fitres$sigma)),
            lapply(seq_len(sim$p), function(i) one_row(sprintf("phi_%d", i), sim$phi[i], fitres$phi[, , i])),
            list(one_row("nu", sim$nu, fitres$nu)))
  tab <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(tab) <- NULL
  attr(tab, "acc_rate") <- mean(fitres$acc_rate)            # block Metropolis acceptance after burn-in
  attr(tab, "sampler") <- "block-mh"                        # marks results from the new sampler
  tab
}

if (!file.exists(val_file) || !identical(attr(readRDS(val_file), "sampler"), "block-mh")) {
  dir.create(dirname(val_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  saveRDS(validate_sampler(), val_file)
}
res_val <- readRDS(val_file)
```


```{r fit-models, include = FALSE}
# ---- Posterior fits for Sections 4-6 ----
#   main         J=2, AR(1) + t innovations, sqrt(kWh), all data: the reported posterior
#   J1           J=1, otherwise identical: does the second harmonic matter?
#   ar2, ar4     AR(2) / AR(4), otherwise identical: is one day of memory enough?
#   kwh          J=2, AR(1) + t innovations on the untransformed kWh scale
#   holdout      main model refitted on data through 2009-11-30, then forecast the final year
#   holdout_ar2, holdout_ar4   the same with AR(2) / AR(4) errors, scored on the same days
# Every fit uses the block random-walk Metropolis sampler of the model-code chunk: eta_t ~ t_nu(0, sigma),
# no latent weights, and missing days left out of the likelihood (conditional likelihood, Section 2.3).
# WAIC is recorded on one shared set of days (observed, with their MAX_LAG previous days observed),
# so differences between models are paired.
# Each fit is saved to results/06_sqrt_mh/<name>.rds and is rerun only if that file is missing.
# (The folder name is new so fits from the old Gibbs sampler in results/06_sqrt/ are never reused.)
# Uses from earlier chunks: d, here(), and the model-code functions.

OUT <- here("results", "06_sqrt_mh")
post_dir <- OUT # later chunks read the saved results from here
MCMC <- list(n_iter = 40000, burn = 10000, thin = 5, n_chains = 4)
TRAIN_END <- as.Date("2009-11-30")
ROLL_H <- 60L
ROLL_STEP <- 3L
MAX_LAG <- 4L   # largest AR order fitted; WAIC uses days whose MAX_LAG previous days are observed

FULL_FITS <- list(
  main     = list(J = 2, p = 1, scale = "sqrt",     seed = 6100, n_paths = 100),
  J1       = list(J = 1, p = 1, scale = "sqrt",     seed = 6200, n_paths = 1),
  ar2      = list(J = 2, p = 2, scale = "sqrt",     seed = 6300, n_paths = 1),
  ar4      = list(J = 2, p = 4, scale = "sqrt",     seed = 6350, n_paths = 1),
  kwh      = list(J = 2, p = 1, scale = "identity", seed = 6400, n_paths = 1)
)
HOLDOUT_FITS <- list(
  holdout     = list(p = 1, seed = 6500),
  holdout_ar2 = list(p = 2, seed = 6600),
  holdout_ar4 = list(p = 4, seed = 6650)
)

run_full <- function(name, d) {
  s <- FULL_FITS[[name]]
  # use the scale's default prior unless this fit overrides it (sensitivity fits)
  tau <- if (is.null(s$prior_tau)) PRIOR_TAU[[s$scale]] else s$prior_tau
  f <- fit_chains(
    d$kwh, d$observed, d$t, d$dow,
    n_chains = MCMC$n_chains, seed = s$seed,
    J = s$J, p = s$p, heavy = TRUE, scale = s$scale,
    n_iter = MCMC$n_iter, burn = MCMC$burn, thin = MCMC$thin,
    # identical WAIC terms for every model, so WAIC differences are paired
    ll_index = common_ll_index(d$observed, max_lag = MAX_LAG),
    n_paths = s$n_paths, disperse_init = TRUE,
    prior_tau = tau
  )
  f$waic <- waic(f$loglik)
  f$loglik <- NULL                 # keep files small: only the WAIC summary is needed
  f$t_center <- mean(d$t)
  f$mcmc <- MCMC
  f$prior_tau <- tau
  f
}

run_holdout <- function(d, p = 1, seed = 6500) {
  train <- d[d$date <= TRAIN_END, ]
  test <- d[d$date > TRAIN_END, ]
  rownames(test) <- NULL
  t_center <- mean(train$t)
  # the 12-month forecast starts from the AR state on the last p training days,
  # which exists only if those days are observed (missing days are not imputed)
  last_p <- nrow(train) - (seq_len(p) - 1L)
  if (!all(train$observed[last_p])) {
    stop(sprintf("The last %d training day(s) before %s include a missing day; move TRAIN_END to an observed run.",
                 p, format(TRAIN_END)))
  }
  f <- fit_chains(
    train$kwh, train$observed, train$t, train$dow,
    n_chains = MCMC$n_chains, seed = seed,
    J = 2, p = p, heavy = TRUE, scale = "sqrt",
    n_iter = MCMC$n_iter, burn = MCMC$burn, thin = MCMC$thin,
    n_paths = 1, disperse_init = TRUE
  )
  f$loglik <- NULL
  scalars <- c(list(f$sigma, f$nu), lapply(seq_len(p), function(i) f$phi[, , i]),
               lapply(seq_along(f$names), function(i) f$beta[, , i]))
  dg <- lapply(scalars, diagnose)
  conv <- c(
    rhat = max(vapply(dg, function(g) max(g$rhat, g$rhat_folded), numeric(1))),
    ess = min(vapply(dg, `[[`, numeric(1), "ess")),
    ess_tail = min(vapply(dg, `[[`, numeric(1), "ess_tail"))
  )

  # A. one 12-month forecast from the last training day
  fc <- forecast(f, test$t, test$dow, t_center, n_draws = 4000, seed = 99)
  q <- apply(fc$y, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))
  single <- data.frame(
    date = test$date, kwh = test$kwh, observed = test$observed,
    lo95 = q[1, ], lo50 = q[2, ], med = q[3, ], hi50 = q[4, ], hi95 = q[5, ],
    crps = crps(fc$y, test$kwh), lpd = log_pred_density(fc, test$kwh), pit = pit(fc, test$kwh)
  )

  # B. rolling origins: from every 3rd holdout day whose day and previous MAX_LAG days are
  #    observed, forecast 1-60 days ahead. Given beta, the AR state at an observed origin is
  #    z_o - x_o'beta, so no refitting is needed. The origin rule does not depend on p, so
  #    every AR order is scored on the same days.
  beta <- flatten(f, "beta")
  set.seed(64)
  sub <- sample.int(nrow(beta), 1500)
  Xtest <- build_design(test$t, test$dow, 2, t_center = t_center)$X
  z_test <- to_model_scale(test$kwh, "sqrt")
  eps_test <- matrix(z_test, nrow(beta), length(z_test), byrow = TRUE) - beta %*% t(Xtest)
  origins <- seq(MAX_LAG, nrow(test) - 1L, by = ROLL_STEP)
  origins <- origins[vapply(origins, function(o) all(test$observed[(o - MAX_LAG + 1L):o]), logical(1))]
  rows <- vector("list", length(origins))
  for (oi in seq_along(origins)) {
    o <- origins[oi]
    idx <- (o + 1L):min(o + ROLL_H, nrow(test))
    fcr <- forecast(f, test$t[idx], test$dow[idx], t_center,
                    eps_init = eps_test[sub, o - (seq_len(p) - 1L), drop = FALSE],
                    draw_idx = sub, seed = 7L * oi)
    qq <- apply(fcr$y, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.75, 0.975))
    rows[[oi]] <- data.frame(
      origin = o, h = seq_along(idx), observed = test$observed[idx], kwh = test$kwh[idx],
      lo95 = qq[1, ], lo50 = qq[2, ], hi50 = qq[3, ], hi95 = qq[4, ],
      crps = crps(fcr$y, test$kwh[idx]), lpd = log_pred_density(fcr, test$kwh[idx])
    )
  }
  list(
    single = single, roll = do.call(rbind, rows), n_origins = length(origins),
    n_train = sum(train$observed), n_test = sum(test$observed),
    train_end = TRAIN_END, phi = matrix(f$phi, ncol = p), conv = conv,
    train_tail = train[train$date > TRAIN_END - 200, c("date", "kwh")]
  )
}

fit_all <- function(d) {
  dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  for (name in c(names(FULL_FITS), names(HOLDOUT_FITS))) {
    path <- file.path(OUT, paste0(name, ".rds"))
    if (file.exists(path)) next                       # already fitted: skip
    t0 <- proc.time()
    res <- if (name %in% names(HOLDOUT_FITS)) {
      run_holdout(d, p = HOLDOUT_FITS[[name]]$p, seed = HOLDOUT_FITS[[name]]$seed)
    } else {
      run_full(name, d)
    }
    saveRDS(res, path)
    message(sprintf("%s done in %.0f s", name, (proc.time() - t0)[["elapsed"]]))
  }
}

fit_all(d)
```


```{r make-results, include = FALSE}
# ---- Tables, figures and numbers for Sections 4-5 ----
# Reads the fits saved by the fit-models chunk (block random-walk Metropolis sampler,
# t_nu(0, sigma) innovations, missing days left out of the likelihood) and writes, to post_dir:
#   summary.rds (every number and figure input used in the text), table_convergence.csv,
#   table_posterior.csv, episodes.csv, horizon.csv.
# Reruns when summary.rds is missing, is an old version, or is older than main.rds.
# Uses from earlier chunks: d, post_dir, here(), and the model-code functions.
# Defines helpers (kwh_curve, dow_full, seas_matrix, param_mats, diag_group, bf_sd) that the
# sensitivity chunk (Section 6) also uses.
#
# All kWh quantities are posterior draws transformed draw by draw. On the square-root scale
# the AR + t error is symmetric about zero, so (x_t' beta)^2 is the median daily consumption
# given the parameters; we call it the typical-day consumption.

IN <- post_dir
ORIGIN <- as.Date("2006-12-17")   # t = 1
DAYNAMES <- c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
CHAIN_COLS <- c("#1f4e79", "#b03a2e", "#148f77", "#b9770e")
NAV <- "#1f4e79"
RED <- "#b03a2e"
WIN <- 14L   # window, in days, of the block-level predictive check

load_fit <- function(name) readRDS(file.path(IN, paste0(name, ".rds")))
q95 <- function(v) unname(quantile(v, c(0.025, 0.975)))
summ <- function(v) c(mean = mean(v), lo = q95(v)[1], hi = q95(v)[2])

# ---------------- convergence helpers ----------------
param_mats <- function(f) {
  out <- list()
  for (i in seq_along(f$names)) out[[f$names[i]]] <- f$beta[, , i]
  out$sigma <- f$sigma
  for (i in seq_len(f$p)) out[[paste0("phi_", i)]] <- f$phi[, , i]
  out$nu <- f$nu
  out
}
diag_group <- function(mats) {
  g <- lapply(mats, diagnose)
  c(rhat = max(vapply(g, function(x) max(x$rhat, x$rhat_folded), numeric(1))),
    ess = min(vapply(g, `[[`, numeric(1), "ess")),
    ess_tail = min(vapply(g, `[[`, numeric(1), "ess_tail")))
}
worst_of <- function(f) diag_group(param_mats(f))   # worst R-hat / smallest ESS over all parameters

# ---------------- kWh-scale summaries of the regression part ----------------
seas_matrix <- function(b, nm, dates, J) {
  tt <- as.numeric(dates - ORIGIN) + 1
  S <- matrix(0, nrow(b), length(dates))
  for (j in seq_len(J)) {
    S <- S + outer(b[, match(paste0("sin_h", j), nm)], sin(2 * pi * j * tt / 365)) +
      outer(b[, match(paste0("cos_h", j), nm)], cos(2 * pi * j * tt / 365))
  }
  S
}
dow_full <- function(b, nm) cbind(0, b[, match(paste0("dow_", DAYNAMES[-1]), nm), drop = FALSE])
# typical-day kWh on each date at the record midpoint, averaged over weekdays
kwh_curve <- function(b, nm, dates, J) {
  dl <- dow_full(b, nm)
  A <- b[, match("intercept", nm)] + seas_matrix(b, nm, dates, J)
  A^2 + 2 * A * rowMeans(dl) + rowMeans(dl^2)
}

# ---------------- Savage-Dickey Bayes factor (used in Sections 5 and 6) ----------------
# BF10 in favour of INCLUDING the coefficients in `cols` (nested model sets them to 0):
#   BF10 = prior density at 0 / posterior density at 0.
# Valid because the coefficient priors are independent normals. The posterior density at 0
# uses a normal approximation from the draws (accurate with ~1,400 days).
# Returned on the log10 scale (e.g. -2 = 100 to 1 in favour of the smaller model).
bf_sd <- function(f, cols) {
  b <- flatten(f, "beta")[, match(cols, f$names), drop = FALSE]
  m <- colMeans(b); Sg <- cov(b); k <- length(cols)
  log_post0 <- -0.5 * k * log(2 * pi) - 0.5 * as.numeric(determinant(Sg)$modulus) -
    0.5 * as.numeric(t(m) %*% solve(Sg, m))
  log_prior0 <- sum(dnorm(0, 0, f$prior_tau[2], log = TRUE))   # SD of the non-intercept coefficients
  (log_prior0 - log_post0) / log(10)
}

make_results <- function(d) {
  f   <- load_fit("main")
  f1  <- load_fit("J1")
  f2  <- load_fit("ar2")
  f4  <- load_fit("ar4")
  fk  <- load_fit("kwh")
  ho  <- load_fit("holdout")
  ho2 <- load_fit("holdout_ar2")
  ho4 <- load_fit("holdout_ar4")
  S <- list()

  # ---------------- Section 4: convergence table ----------------
  n_chain <- dim(f$beta)[1]
  n_draw <- dim(f$beta)[2]
  pm <- param_mats(f)
  acc <- mean(f$acc_rate)            # one acceptance rate for the whole block
  groups <- list(
    list("Regression coefficients (12)", "Block random-walk Metropolis", pm[f$names]),
    list("Innovation scale $\\sigma$", "Same block, on $\\log\\sigma$", pm["sigma"]),
    list("Autoregressive coefficient $\\phi$", "Same block", pm["phi_1"]),
    list("Degrees of freedom $\\nu$", "Same block, on $\\log(\\nu - 2)$", pm["nu"])
  )
  conv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(g) {
    dg <- diag_group(g[[3]])
    data.frame(
      Parameters = g[[1]], Update = g[[2]],
      Acceptance = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * acc),
      `Worst R-hat` = sprintf("%.3f", dg[["rhat"]]),
      `Min bulk ESS` = sprintf("%.0f", dg[["ess"]]),
      `Min tail ESS` = sprintf("%.0f", dg[["ess_tail"]]),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }))
  write.csv(conv, file.path(IN, "table_convergence.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  all_main <- worst_of(f)
  S$conv <- list(
    table = conv,  # Table 8 rows (block Metropolis)
    n_chain = n_chain, n_draw_per_chain = n_draw, n_total = n_chain * n_draw,
    mcmc = f$mcmc, acc = acc, worst = all_main,
    mcse_max_frac = 1 / sqrt(all_main[["ess"]]),
    others = rbind(J1 = worst_of(f1), ar2 = worst_of(f2), ar4 = worst_of(f4), kwh = worst_of(fk)),
    holdout = rbind(ar1 = ho$conv, ar2 = ho2$conv, ar4 = ho4$conv)
  )

  # ---------------- Figure 6 inputs: trace plots with burn-in ----------------
  show <- list(
    list(key = "trend_per_year", lab = expression(beta[1] ~ "(trend)")),
    list(key = "sigma", lab = expression(sigma)),
    list(key = "phi_1", lab = expression(phi)),
    list(key = "nu", lab = expression(nu))
  )
  warm_names <- c("sigma", "nu", paste0("phi_", seq_len(f$p)), f$names)
  S$fig6 <- list(
    trace = lapply(setNames(show, vapply(show, `[[`, "", "key")), function(s) list(
      warm = f$warmup[, , match(s$key, warm_names)],   # burn-in draws, chains x iterations
      post = pm[[s$key]]                               # kept draws, chains x draws
    )),
    thin = f$mcmc$thin, burn = f$mcmc$burn, n_chain = n_chain
  )

  # ---------------- Section 5: posterior quantities ----------------
  b <- flatten(f, "beta")
  nm <- f$names
  yr <- seq(as.Date("2009-01-01"), as.Date("2009-12-31"), by = "day")
  win <- seq(as.Date("2009-07-01"), as.Date("2010-06-30"), by = "day")
  M2 <- kwh_curve(b, nm, yr, 2)
  annual <- rowMeans(M2)
  Mw <- kwh_curve(b, nm, win, 2)
  peak_kwh <- apply(Mw, 1, max)
  peak_day <- win[apply(Mw, 1, which.max)]
  trough_kwh <- apply(M2, 1, min)
  trough_day <- yr[apply(M2, 1, which.min)]
  pk_q <- sort(peak_day)[round(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975) * length(peak_day))]
  tr_q <- sort(trough_day)[round(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975) * length(trough_day))]

  # what the second harmonic adds, inside the J = 2 posterior
  M1_in <- kwh_curve(b, nm, yr, 1)
  add2 <- apply(abs(M2 - M1_in), 1, max)
  amp <- function(j) sqrt(b[, match(paste0("sin_h", j), nm)]^2 + b[, match(paste0("cos_h", j), nm)]^2)
  ratio21 <- amp(2) / amp(1)
  b1 <- flatten(f1, "beta")
  M1_model <- kwh_curve(b1, f1$names, yr, 1)

  # WAIC differences on the shared set of days (positive favours the first model)
  paired <- function(a, z) {
    di <- a$waic$elpd_i - z$waic$elpd_i
    c(diff = sum(di), se = sqrt(length(di) * var(di)))
  }
  S$waic <- list(
    J2_vs_J1 = paired(f, f1), ar2_vs_ar1 = paired(f2, f), ar4_vs_ar1 = paired(f4, f),
    sqrt_vs_kwh = paired(f, fk),
    p_waic = c(main = f$waic$p_waic, J1 = f1$waic$p_waic, ar2 = f2$waic$p_waic,
               ar4 = f4$waic$p_waic, kwh = fk$waic$p_waic),
    n = f$waic$n
  )

  # trend: the change per year in the annual-mean typical day is 2 * beta1 * mean(x'beta)
  dl <- dow_full(b, nm)
  A <- b[, match("intercept", nm)] + seas_matrix(b, nm, yr, 2)
  b_tr <- b[, match("trend_per_year", nm)]
  slope_kwh <- 2 * b_tr * (rowMeans(A) + rowMeans(dl))
  slope_pct <- 100 * slope_kwh / annual
  years <- (nrow(d) - 1) / 365

  # weekly profile in kWh, averaged over the year
  a1 <- rowMeans(A)
  a2 <- rowMeans(A^2)
  E <- a2 + 2 * dl * a1 + dl^2
  P <- E - rowMeans(E)
  wkend <- rowMeans(P[, 6:7]) - rowMeans(P[, 1:5])

  phi <- as.numeric(f$phi)

  S$post <- list(
    annual = summ(annual),
    slope_kwh = summ(slope_kwh), slope_pct = summ(slope_pct),
    total_change = summ(years * slope_kwh), years = years,
    p_decline = mean(b_tr < 0), p_rope1 = mean(abs(slope_pct) < 1),
    peak_kwh = summ(peak_kwh), peak_day = pk_q, trough_kwh = summ(trough_kwh), trough_day = tr_q,
    swing = summ(peak_kwh - trough_kwh), peak_ratio = summ(peak_kwh / trough_kwh),
    amp_ratio = summ(ratio21), add2 = summ(add2), p_add2_gt1 = mean(add2 > 1),
    J1_vs_J2_curve_maxdiff = max(abs(colMeans(M2) - colMeans(M1_model))),
    J1_vs_J2_where = yr[which.max(abs(colMeans(M2) - colMeans(M1_model)))],
    dow = lapply(setNames(seq_along(DAYNAMES), DAYNAMES), function(k) summ(P[, k])),
    wkend = summ(wkend), p_wkend = mean(wkend > 0),
    p_thu_lowest = mean(apply(P, 1, which.min) == 4),
    sigma = summ(as.numeric(f$sigma)), phi = summ(phi), nu = summ(as.numeric(f$nu)),
    sd_ratio = summ(1 / sqrt(1 - phi^2))
  )

  fmt3 <- function(s, dp = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f [%.", dp, "f, %.", dp, "f]"), s[1], s[2], s[3])
  pd <- S$post
  dfmt <- function(x) sub("^0", "", format(x, "%d %b"))
  post_tab <- data.frame(
    Question = c("Level", "Long-term trend", "", "Annual cycle", "", "", "",
                 "Weekly pattern", "", "Day-to-day memory", "Tail weight"),
    Quantity = c(
      "Typical-day consumption, annual mean (kWh/day)",
      "Change in annual mean (kWh/day per year)",
      "Same, as % per year",
      sprintf("Winter peak (kWh/day), median date %s", dfmt(pd$peak_day[2])),
      sprintf("Summer trough (kWh/day), median date %s", dfmt(pd$trough_day[2])),
      "Peak-to-trough swing (kWh/day)",
      "Largest change from adding the second harmonic (kWh/day)",
      "Weekend minus weekday (kWh/day)",
      "Thursday versus the weekly mean (kWh/day)",
      "AR(1) coefficient $\\phi$",
      "Degrees of freedom $\\nu$"
    ),
    `Posterior mean [95% CrI]` = c(
      fmt3(pd$annual), fmt3(pd$slope_kwh, 2), fmt3(pd$slope_pct), fmt3(pd$peak_kwh),
      fmt3(pd$trough_kwh), fmt3(pd$swing), fmt3(pd$add2), fmt3(pd$wkend), fmt3(pd$dow$Thu),
      fmt3(pd$phi, 2), fmt3(pd$nu)
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  write.csv(post_tab, file.path(IN, "table_posterior.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  S$post_tab <- post_tab

  # ---------------- Figure 7 inputs: annual cycle and weekly pattern ----------------
  mq <- apply(M2, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  m1q <- apply(M1_model, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  obs <- d[d$observed, ]
  mon <- as.integer(format(obs$date, "%m"))
  mon_med <- tapply(obs$kwh, mon, median)
  mids <- as.Date(sprintf("2009-%02d-15", 1:12))
  pq <- apply(P, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  S$fig7 <- list(yr = yr, mq = mq, m1q = m1q, mids = mids, mon_med = mon_med, pq = pq)

  # ---------------- forecasting (holdout) ----------------
  r <- ho$roll[ho$roll$observed, ]
  r$w95 <- r$hi95 - r$lo95
  r$c95 <- r$kwh >= r$lo95 & r$kwh <= r$hi95
  r$c50 <- r$kwh >= r$lo50 & r$kwh <= r$hi50
  byh <- aggregate(cbind(w95, c95, c50, crps) ~ h, data = r, FUN = mean)
  sg <- ho$single[ho$single$observed, ]
  S$fc <- list(
    n_train = ho$n_train, n_test = ho$n_test, n_origins = ho$n_origins, train_end = ho$train_end,
    byh = byh,
    single = c(c95 = mean(sg$kwh >= sg$lo95 & sg$kwh <= sg$hi95),
               c50 = mean(sg$kwh >= sg$lo50 & sg$kwh <= sg$hi50),
               crps = mean(sg$crps), mae = mean(abs(sg$kwh - sg$med)), w95 = mean(sg$hi95 - sg$lo95)),
    phi_holdout = mean(ho$phi), theory_ratio = 1 / sqrt(1 - mean(ho$phi)^2)
  )

  # higher AR orders versus AR(1) on identical held-out forecasts (positive favours the higher order)
  key <- function(z) paste(z$origin, z$h)
  per_origin <- function(v) {           # forecasts from one origin overlap: average within origin first
    m <- tapply(v, r$origin, mean)
    c(diff = mean(m), se = sd(m) / sqrt(length(m)))
  }
  compare_ar <- function(hoX) {
    rX <- hoX$roll[hoX$roll$observed, ]
    stopifnot(identical(key(r), key(rX)))
    sX <- hoX$single[hoX$single$observed, ]
    list(roll_lpd = per_origin(rX$lpd - r$lpd), roll_crps = per_origin(r$crps - rX$crps),
         single_lpd = mean(sX$lpd - sg$lpd), single_crps = mean(sg$crps - sX$crps),
         phi = colMeans(hoX$phi))
  }
  S$ar_order <- list(ar2 = compare_ar(ho2), ar4 = compare_ar(ho4))
  write.csv(byh, file.path(IN, "horizon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  S$fig8 <- list(s1 = ho$single, tr = ho$train_tail, byh = byh, train_end = ho$train_end)

  # ---------------- Q6: unusual days and periods ----------------
  od <- one_step_diagnostics(f, NULL, d$observed)
  wt <- od$wt_mean                                  # implied t weight per day (NA if not in the likelihood)
  low_w <- d$observed & !is.na(wt) & wt < 0.5       # days the t likelihood gives under half weight
  sgn <- sign(od$std_resid_mean)
  absence <- rep(FALSE, nrow(d))
  rl <- rle(d$observed & d$kwh < 12)
  ends <- cumsum(rl$lengths)
  for (i in which(rl$values & rl$lengths >= 5)) absence[(ends[i] - rl$lengths[i] + 1):ends[i]] <- TRUE
  ok <- is.finite(od$ppp)

  # block-level check: each 14-day mean against replicated series from the
  # fitted model (systematic part plus a stationary AR(1) error with t innovations)
  pp <- f$path_pars
  n_paths <- nrow(pp)
  per_chain <- n_paths / n_chain
  path_every <- max(1L, n_draw %/% per_chain)
  rows_b <- as.vector(outer((seq_len(per_chain) - 1L) * path_every + 1L, (seq_len(n_chain) - 1L) * n_draw, `+`))
  set.seed(3)
  mu_s <- b[rows_b, , drop = FALSE] %*% t(f$X)
  nT <- ncol(mu_s)
  sig_s <- pp[, 1]; nu_s <- pp[, 2]; phi_s <- pp[, 4]
  eta_s <- matrix(rt(n_paths * nT, df = rep(nu_s, nT)), n_paths, nT) * sig_s   # t_nu(0, sigma) innovations
  eps_s <- matrix(0, n_paths, nT)
  eps_s[, 1] <- eta_s[, 1] / sqrt(1 - phi_s^2)
  for (i in 2:nT) eps_s[, i] <- phi_s * eps_s[, i - 1] + eta_s[, i]
  y_rep <- pmax(mu_s + eps_s, 0)^2
  y_rep[, !d$observed] <- NA
  roll <- function(v) {
    k <- stats::filter(as.numeric(!is.na(v)), rep(1, WIN), sides = 1)
    s <- stats::filter(ifelse(is.na(v), 0, v), rep(1, WIN), sides = 1)
    ifelse(k >= 0.7 * WIN, s / pmax(k, 1), NA_real_)
  }
  obs_roll <- roll(d$kwh)
  rep_roll <- t(apply(y_rep, 1, roll))
  p_blk <- colMeans(rep_roll <= rep(obs_roll, each = n_paths), na.rm = TRUE)
  p_blk[!is.finite(obs_roll)] <- NA
  flag <- is.finite(p_blk) & (p_blk < 0.01 | p_blk > 0.99)
  dir_hi <- p_blk > 0.5
  fitted_typ <- colMeans(pmax(b %*% t(f$X), 0)^2)
  eps_rows <- list()
  i <- 1L
  while (i <= nT) {
    if (isTRUE(flag[i])) {
      j <- i
      while (j + 1L <= nT && isTRUE(flag[j + 1L]) && dir_hi[j + 1L] == dir_hi[i]) j <- j + 1L
      lo <- max(1L, i - WIN + 1L)
      eps_rows[[length(eps_rows) + 1]] <- c(lo, j, as.integer(dir_hi[i]))
      i <- j + 1L
    } else i <- i + 1L
  }
  merged <- list()
  for (e in eps_rows) {
    k <- length(merged)
    if (k && merged[[k]][3] == e[3] && e[1] <= merged[[k]][2] + 1) merged[[k]][2] <- max(merged[[k]][2], e[2])
    else merged[[k + 1]] <- e
  }
  episodes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(merged, function(e) {
    ix <- e[1]:e[2]
    data.frame(
      from = d$date[e[1]], to = d$date[e[2]], days = length(ix),
      direction = if (e[3] == 1) "high" else "low",
      observed_kwh = mean(d$kwh[ix], na.rm = TRUE), typical_kwh = mean(fitted_typ[ix]),
      in_absence_block = mean(absence[ix])
    )
  }))
  episodes$ratio <- episodes$observed_kwh / episodes$typical_kwh
  write.csv(episodes, file.path(IN, "episodes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  S$q6 <- list(
    n_eval = sum(ok), ppp_lo = sum(od$ppp[ok] < 0.01), ppp_hi = sum(od$ppp[ok] > 0.99),
    n_low_weight = sum(low_w), n_low_weight_high = sum(low_w & sgn > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_low_weight_low = sum(low_w & sgn < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    absence_days = sum(absence), absence_low_weight = sum(low_w & absence),
    wt_absence_mean = mean(wt[absence], na.rm = TRUE), wt_other_mean = mean(wt[d$observed & !absence], na.rm = TRUE),
    n_windows = sum(is.finite(p_blk)), n_flag_lo = sum(p_blk < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_flag_hi = sum(p_blk > 0.99, na.rm = TRUE), episodes = episodes
  )
  S$fig9 <- list(fitted_typ = fitted_typ, low_w = low_w, episodes = episodes)

  saveRDS(S, file.path(IN, "summary.rds"))
  invisible(S)
}


sum_file <- file.path(IN, "summary.rds")
needs_rerun <- !file.exists(sum_file) ||
  any(vapply(c("fig6", "fig7", "fig8", "fig9"), function(k) is.null(readRDS(sum_file)[[k]]), logical(1))) ||
  is.null(readRDS(sum_file)$conv$table) ||   # old summary without the new Table 8
  file.mtime(file.path(IN, "main.rds")) > file.mtime(sum_file)     # main was refit after the summary
if (needs_rerun) make_results(d)
S <- readRDS(sum_file)   # every number and figure input used in Sections 4-5
```

# show the result of validating the sampler on simulated data
val_show <- res_val
val_show[, c("Truth", "Posterior mean", "2.5%", "97.5%", "R-hat")] <-
  round(val_show[, c("Truth", "Posterior mean", "2.5%", "97.5%", "R-hat")], 3)
val_show$ESS <- round(val_show$ESS)
val_show$Covered <- ifelse(val_show$Covered, "yes", "no")
knitr::kable(val_show, align = "lrrrrcrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf(paste("Table 7. Sampler validation on a series simulated from the model","(square-root scale, AR(1) errors, $t$ innovations), with the same 23 days","missing and left out of the likelihood. Block random-walk Metropolis,","%.0f%% of proposals accepted after burn-in. %d of %d 95%% credible","intervals cover the true value."),100 * attr(res_val, "acc_rate"), sum(res_val$Covered), nrow(res_val)))

```{r brms-check, include = FALSE}
# ---- Independent cross-check of the custom sampler with brms (Stan's No-U-Turn sampler) ----
# Refits the final model (J = 2, AR(1) errors, Student-t innovations eta_t ~ t_nu(0, sigma),
# sqrt kWh, same priors) with brms. As in our sampler there are no latent weights (brms's
# student() family uses the t density directly) and the 23 missing days are left out:
# the data are split into runs of consecutive observed days, and ar(gr = run) restarts the
# AR process after every gap, so no day is linked across a gap and nothing is imputed.
# Then measures how far brms's posterior means are from ours, in units of our posterior SD.
# The fit is saved to results/brms/main_runs.rds (first run ~5-10 min; later knits load it).
# Uses from earlier chunks: d, here(), build_design, flatten, load_fit.
library(brms)                                         # uses the cmdstanr backend installed earlier
dir.create(here("results", "brms"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# data: the SAME 12 predictor columns and names as our sampler, observed days only
des <- build_design(d$t, d$dow, J = 2)                # intercept, trend_per_year, sin_h1, ..., dow_Sun
nm  <- des$names
bd  <- setNames(data.frame(des$X), nm)
bd$z   <- sqrt(d$kwh)                                  # response on the sqrt scale
bd$t   <- d$t                                          # day index: tells ar() the time order
bd$run <- cumsum(!d$observed)                          # run id: changes at every missing day
bd     <- bd[d$observed, ]                             # missing days left out (no imputation)

# model: same mean structure; ar(cov = FALSE) puts phi * yesterday's residual in the mean,
# so the Student-t likelihood applies to the innovation eta_t; gr = run restarts it after each gap
form <- as.formula(paste("z ~ 0 +", paste(nm, collapse = " + "),
                         "+ ar(time = t, gr = run, p = 1, cov = FALSE)"))
fit_b <- brm(form, data = bd, family = student(),
             prior = c(prior(normal(0, 20), class = b, coef = intercept),  # Section 3 priors
                       prior(normal(0, 5),  class = b),
                       prior(student_t(3, 0, 2), class = sigma),          # half-t3(0, 2)
                       prior(exponential(0.1), class = nu)),              # brms: nu - 1 ~ Exp(mean 10); ours: nu - 2
             chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, cores = 4, seed = 638,
             backend = "cmdstanr", refresh = 0, file = here("results", "brms", "main_runs"))

# compare: posterior means of all 15 parameters (12 coefficients, sigma, phi, nu)
fc   <- load_fit("main")                               # our sampler's main fit (Section 4)
cust <- cbind(flatten(fc, "beta"), flatten(fc, "sigma"), flatten(fc, "phi"), flatten(fc, "nu"))
vars <- c(paste0("b_", nm), "sigma", "ar[1]", "nu")    # brms names, same order
bm   <- as.matrix(fit_b, variable = vars)
gap  <- abs(colMeans(bm) - colMeans(cust)) / apply(cust, 2, sd)   # difference in posterior SDs

# brms's own convergence checks
sb <- posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit_b, variable = vars))
np <- nuts_params(fit_b)
vb <- list(gap  = sprintf("%.2f", max(gap)),
           rhat = sprintf("%.3f", max(sb$rhat)),
           div  = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"]))      # divergent transitions (want 0)
```

```{r}
# DELETE BEFORE KNITTING!
vb                         # the three numbers used in the text: gap, worst R-hat, divergences
round(gap, 3)              # difference for each of the 15 parameters, in posterior SDs
summary(fit_b)             # brms's own table: estimates, Rhat, Bulk_ESS, Tail_ESS
prior_summary(fit_b)       # confirm the priors brms actually used (incl. the ar prior)
file.exists(here("results", "brms", "main.rds"))   # TRUE = the fit was saved
```
The posterior has no closed form, so we sample it with a Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler written for this model, following Chib (1993) for the autoregressive errors and Geweke (1993) for the $t$ errors. Three augmentations make most full conditionals standard: each $t$ error is a normal error with a latent weight, $\eta_t \mid \lambda_t \sim N(0, \sigma^2/\lambda_t)$ with $\lambda_t \sim \text{Gamma}(\nu/2, \nu/2)$; the half-$t$ prior on $\sigma$ is an inverse-gamma mixture; and the 23 missing days are treated as unknowns. Each iteration draws $\beta$ from a multivariate normal, $\sigma^2$ from an inverse gamma, each $\lambda_t$ from a gamma, and each missing day from a normal. $\phi$ and $\nu$ have no standard full conditional, so they take random-walk Metropolis steps, rejecting non-stationary $\phi$. All parameters are updated together by one block random-walk Metropolis step on $(\beta, \log\sigma, \phi, \log(\nu-2))$, with a proposal covariance taken from the curvature of the log posterior at its mode; after tuning during burn-in, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * S$conv$acc)%` of proposals are accepted (Table 8).

We ran four chains of 40,000 iterations from dispersed starting values, discarded the first 10,000, and kept every fifth draw, leaving 24,000 draws. The worst rank-normalized split-$\hat{R}$ is `r sprintf("%.3f", S$conv$worst[["rhat"]])` and the smallest effective sample size (ESS) is `r round(S$conv$worst[["ess"]])` (Vehtari et al., 2021), against targets of 1.01 and 400, so Monte Carlo error is at most about `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * S$conv$mcse_max_frac)`% of a posterior standard deviation. In Figure 6, every chain reaches the same region within about 1,000 iterations, well inside the discarded burn-in, and the chains' densities overlap.

On data simulated with known parameters, the 95% intervals covered `r sum(res_val$Covered)` of `r nrow(res_val)` true values (Table 7). The misses are the Thursday and Friday effects, adjacent days whose estimates are correlated through the AR(1) errors, and $\sigma$, whose interval ends just below its true value. Refitting the real data with brms (Bürkner, 2017), which uses Stan's No-U-Turn sampler instead of Gibbs, gives the same posterior: the posterior means of all 12 coefficients, $\sigma$, $\phi$ and $\nu$ lie within `r vb$gap` posterior standard deviations of ours (worst $\hat{R}$ `r vb$rhat`, `r vb$div` divergent transitions).

# 5. Posterior Results and Interpretation

```{r sec5-numbers, include = FALSE}
# numbers quoted in Section 5, all taken from S (make-results chunk) and the main fit
# (block random-walk Metropolis; t_nu(0, sigma) innovations; missing days left out of the likelihood)
fmt_n   <- function(x, dp = 1) gsub("-", "\u2212", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = dp, big.mark = ","))
fmt_ci  <- function(s, dp = 1) sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", fmt_n(s[1], dp), fmt_n(s[2], dp), fmt_n(s[3], dp))
fmt_day <- function(x) paste(as.integer(format(x, "%d")), format(x, "%B"))
bf_word <- function(b) c("barely any", "substantial", "strong", "decisive")[findInterval(abs(b), c(0, 0.5, 1, 2))]  # Kass & Raftery (1995)
pct_rng <- function(r) if (length(r)) paste(fmt_n(100 * range(r), 0), collapse = "\u2013") else "n/a"

pd <- S$post; fc <- S$fc; q6 <- S$q6; hz <- fc$byh
ep <- q6$episodes
if (is.null(ep)) ep <- data.frame(from = as.Date(character()), direction = character(),
                                  in_absence_block = numeric(), ratio = numeric())   # no episode flagged
fm <- load_fit("main"); if (is.null(fm$prior_tau)) fm$prior_tau <- PRIOR_TAU$sqrt
bf_tr <- bf_sd(fm, "trend_per_year")                 # log10 BF10 for the trend (same as Table 11)
bf_h2 <- bf_sd(fm, c("sin_h2", "cos_h2"))            # log10 BF10 for the second harmonic
ep_abs <- ep[ep$direction == "low" & ep$in_absence_block > 0, ]   # low episodes during absence blocks
ep_hi  <- ep[ep$direction == "high", ]

v <- list(
  annual = fmt_ci(pd$annual),
  slope = fmt_ci(pd$slope_kwh, 2), slope_pct = fmt_ci(pd$slope_pct),
  p_decline = sprintf("%.2f", pd$p_decline),
  bf_tr = fmt_n(bf_tr), bf_tr_txt = paste(bf_word(bf_tr), "evidence", if (bf_tr < 0) "against" else "for", "a trend"),
  peak = fmt_ci(pd$peak_kwh), peak_day = fmt_day(pd$peak_day[2]),
  trough = fmt_ci(pd$trough_kwh), trough_day = fmt_day(pd$trough_day[2]),
  swing = fmt_n(pd$swing[1]), add2 = fmt_ci(pd$add2),
  waic_J = fmt_n(S$waic$J2_vs_J1[["diff"]]), waic_J_se = fmt_n(S$waic$J2_vs_J1[["se"]]),
  bf_h2 = fmt_n(bf_h2),
  wkend = fmt_ci(pd$wkend),
  wkend_p = if (pd$p_wkend == 1) "in every posterior draw" else
              sprintf("with posterior probability %.3f", pd$p_wkend),
  thu = fmt_ci(-pd$dow$Thu[c(1, 3, 2)]),             # "below the mean": flip sign, swap interval ends
  w1 = fmt_n(hz$w95[hz$h == 1]),
  w3 = paste(fmt_n(range(hz$w95[hz$h >= 3]), 0), collapse = "\u2013"),
  sd_ratio = fmt_n(pd$sd_ratio[1], 2), phi = fmt_ci(pd$phi, 2),
  c95 = fmt_n(100 * mean(hz$c95)), c50 = fmt_n(100 * mean(hz$c50), 0),
  cal = if (mean(hz$c95) > 0.96) "slightly conservative" else "well calibrated",
  mae = fmt_n(fc$single[["mae"]]), mae_pct = fmt_n(100 * fc$single[["mae"]] / pd$annual[1], 0),
  n_flag = q6$ppp_lo + q6$ppp_hi, n_eval = fmt_n(q6$n_eval, 0), n_exp = round(0.02 * q6$n_eval),
  nu = fmt_ci(pd$nu),
  n_lowW = q6$n_low_weight,                          # days whose implied t weight (nu+1)/(nu+eta^2/sigma^2) < 1/2
  n_ep = nrow(ep), n_ep_lo = sum(ep$direction == "low"),
  n_abs = nrow(ep_abs), abs_pct = pct_rng(ep_abs$ratio),
  n_ep_hi = nrow(ep_hi), hi_verb = if (nrow(ep_hi) == 1) "is" else "are",
  hi_dates = if (nrow(ep_hi)) paste(format(ep_hi$from, "%B %Y"), collapse = " and ") else "none"
)
```

We summarize each draw on the kWh scale through the *typical day*, $(x_t^\top\beta)^2$, which is the median daily consumption given the parameters because the error is symmetric on the square-root scale (Table 9).

```{r table9, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  S$post_tab, escape = FALSE, align = "llr",row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste(
    "Table 9. Posterior means and 95% credible intervals (CrI). kWh quantities refer to the typical day",
    "at the record midpoint, averaged over the week or the year as appropriate."
  )
)
```

**Variation and trend (Q1, Q2).** A typical day uses `r v$annual` kWh (posterior mean [95% CrI]), and use varies seasonally, weekly, and from day to day around this level. The annual mean changes by `r v$slope` kWh per year, or `r v$slope_pct`% per year. A decline has posterior probability `r v$p_decline`, but the interval includes zero, and the Savage–Dickey Bayes factor is $\log_{10}\text{BF}_{10} =$ `r v$bf_tr`, `r v$bf_tr_txt` (Section 6). Consumption did not drift over the four years ( OR there is no significant long-term increase or decrease).

**Annual cycle (Q3).** Typical use peaks at `r v$peak` kWh around `r v$peak_day` and falls to `r v$trough` kWh around `r v$trough_day`, a swing of `r v$swing` kWh (Figure 7a). The second harmonic flattens late winter and deepens the summer trough, moving the curve by up to `r v$add2` kWh. It raises WAIC's expected log predictive density by `r v$waic_J` (SE `r v$waic_J_se`), and its Bayes factor is $\log_{10}\text{BF}_{10} =$ `r v$bf_h2` (about $10^{5}$ to 1 in favour of the second harmonic).

**Weekly pattern (Q4).** Weekends use `r v$wkend` kWh more than weekdays, `r v$wkend_p`. Thursday is the lowest weekday, `r v$thu` kWh below the weekly mean (Figure 7b).

```{r fig7, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 4.4, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Figure 7. (a) Posterior typical-day consumption over the year with 95% credible bands, for the final two-harmonic model and the one-harmonic model; dots are observed monthly medians. (b) Day-of-week effects relative to the weekly mean, with 95% credible intervals."}
local({
  p <- S$fig7
  layout(matrix(1:2, nrow = 1), widths = c(1.7, 1))
  par(mar = c(3, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
  plot(p$yr, p$mq[2, ], type = "n", ylim = range(c(p$mq, p$m1q, p$mon_med)), xlab = "",
       ylab = "typical-day kWh", main = "(a) Annual cycle", las = 1, xaxt = "n")
  axis(1, at = p$mids, labels = substr(month.abb, 1, 1))
  polygon(c(p$yr, rev(p$yr)), c(p$mq[1, ], rev(p$mq[3, ])), col = adjustcolor(NAV, 0.22), border = NA)
  polygon(c(p$yr, rev(p$yr)), c(p$m1q[1, ], rev(p$m1q[3, ])), col = adjustcolor(RED, 0.15), border = NA)
  lines(p$yr, p$mq[2, ], col = NAV, lwd = 2)
  lines(p$yr, p$m1q[2, ], col = RED, lwd = 1.6, lty = 2)
  points(p$mids, p$mon_med, pch = 16, cex = 0.8)
  legend("bottomleft", legend = c("two harmonics (final model)", "one harmonic", "observed monthly median"),
         col = c(NAV, RED, "black"), lwd = c(2, 1.6, NA), lty = c(1, 2, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, 16),
         bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
  plot(1:7, p$pq[2, ], ylim = range(p$pq), pch = 16, col = NAV, xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
       ylab = "kWh/day vs weekly mean", main = "(b) Day of week", las = 1)
  arrows(1:7, p$pq[1, ], 1:7, p$pq[3, ], angle = 90, code = 3, length = 0.04, col = NAV)
  axis(1, at = 1:7, labels = DAYNAMES)
  abline(h = 0, lty = 3)
})
```

**Forecasting (Q5).** Refitting through November 2009 and forecasting the final year (Figure 8), the mean 95% interval is `r v$w1` kWh wide one day ahead and `r v$w3` kWh from day three onward, close to the limit $1/\sqrt{1-\phi^2} =$ `r v$sd_ratio` implied by $\phi =$ `r v$phi`, so after a few days forecasts reduce to the seasonal and weekly pattern. The intervals are `r v$cal` (`r v$c95`% and `r v$c50`% coverage at the 95% and 50% levels) but wide: the 12-month forecast misses by `r v$mae` kWh per day on average, about `r v$mae_pct`% of typical use.

```{r fig8, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7.5, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = paste0("Figure 8. Forecasting the held-out final year from a fit through ", format(S$fc$train_end, "%d %B %Y"), ". (a) Twelve-month predictive median with 50% and 95% intervals against actual consumption; (b) mean 95% interval width and (c) empirical coverage by horizon, over ", S$fc$n_origins, " rolling forecast origins.")}

       ylim = c(yl[1], yl[2] * 1.15), xlab = "", ylab = "kWh/day",
       main = sprintf("(a) Forecast of the final year from %s (dashed line: end of training data)",
                      format(p$train_end, "%d %b %Y")), las = 1)
  polygon(c(s1$date, rev(s1$date)), c(s1$lo95, rev(s1$hi95)), col = adjustcolor(NAV, 0.2), border = NA)
  polygon(c(s1$date, rev(s1$date)), c(s1$lo50, rev(s1$hi50)), col = adjustcolor(NAV, 0.35), border = NA)
  lines(s1$date, s1$med, col = NAV, lwd = 1.4)
  points(s1$date, s1$kwh, pch = 16, cex = 0.35, col = RED)
  abline(v = p$train_end, lty = 2)
  legend("topright", legend = c("training data", "50% / 95% predictive interval", "predictive median", "held-out actual"),
         col = c("grey35", adjustcolor(NAV, 0.5), NAV, RED), lty = c(1, NA, 1, NA), pch = c(NA, 15, NA, 16),
         pt.cex = c(NA, 1.6, NA, 0.8), bty = "n", cex = 0.8, ncol = 4)
  plot(byh$h, byh$w95, type = "b", pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = NAV, ylim = c(0, max(byh$w95) * 1.08),

  plot(byh$h, 100 * byh$c95, type = "b", pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = NAV, ylim = c(30, 100),
       xlab = "forecast horizon (days ahead)", ylab = "empirical coverage (%)",
       main = "(c) Calibration by horizon", las = 1)
  lines(byh$h, 100 * byh$c50, type = "b", pch = 1, cex = 0.5, col = RED)
  abline(h = c(95, 50), lty = 2, col = c(NAV, RED))
  legend("right", legend = c("95% interval", "50% interval"), col = c(NAV, RED), pch = c(16, 1), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
})
```

**Unexplained periods (Q6).** Single unusual days occur about as often as chance predicts: `r v$n_flag` of `r v$n_eval` one-step-ahead predictive p-values fall below 0.01 or above 0.99, against `r v$n_exp` expected. The $t$ errors ($\nu =$ `r v$nu`) give `r v$n_lowW` isolated extreme days less than half weight, but not the absence blocks, whose low level the AR(1) term carries forward. Sustained periods are not explained: comparing each 14-day mean with its posterior predictive distribution flags `r v$n_ep` episodes (Figure 9). `r v$n_ep_lo` are low, `r v$n_abs` of them during absence blocks, when use fell to `r v$abs_pct`% of a typical day; `r v$n_ep_hi` `r v$hi_verb` high (`r v$hi_dates`). Calendar terms cannot anticipate these behavioral episodes.

```{r fig9, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 4.4, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Figure 9. Observed consumption against the model's typical day. Shading marks 14-day periods whose mean falls outside the central 98% of its posterior predictive distribution; circles mark days whose weight under the t likelihood, (ν + 1)/(ν + η²/σ²), is below 1/2."}

  p <- S$fig9; low_w <- p$low_w
