  plot(d$date, d$kwh, type = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "kWh/day", las = 1,
       ylim = c(0, 1.12 * max(d$kwh, na.rm = TRUE)),
       main = "Periods the fitted model does not explain (14-day predictive check)")
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(episodes))) {
    rect(episodes$from[k], par("usr")[3], episodes$to[k], par("usr")[4], border = NA,
         col = adjustcolor(if (episodes$direction[k] == "high") RED else NAV, 0.18))
  }
  lines(d$date, d$kwh, col = "grey45", lwd = 0.5)                     # breaks at missing days
  lines(d$date, stats::filter(p$fitted_typ, rep(1 / 7, 7), sides = 2), col = "black", lwd = 1.6)
  points(d$date[low_w], d$kwh[low_w], pch = 1, cex = 0.55, col = RED)
  legend("topright", legend = c("observed", "typical day from the model (7-day mean)", "t-likelihood weight below 1/2",
                                "unusually high period", "unusually low period"),
         col = c("grey45", "black", RED, adjustcolor(RED, 0.4), adjustcolor(NAV, 0.4)),
         lty = c(1, 1, NA, NA, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, 1, 15, 15), pt.cex = c(NA, NA, 0.8, 1.8, 1.8),

# 6. Sensitivity Analysis and Model Checking

```{r sensitivity, include = FALSE}
# ---- Section 6 ----
# A. Prior sensitivity: refit the final model (J = 2, AR(1) errors, t_nu(0, sigma) innovations,
#    sqrt kWh) on all data, changing one prior at a time. Same sampler (block random-walk
#    Metropolis), seed, MCMC settings and likelihood (missing days left out) as `main`, so any
#    difference comes from the prior (nu_light runs twice as long, since a prior that allows
#    large nu spreads its posterior further).
# B. Savage-Dickey Bayes factors for the trend and the second harmonic under every prior.
# C. Posterior predictive checks: whole series replicated from the posterior, six statistics.
# D. Coverage of the held-out predictive intervals by season.
# Refits are saved to results/09_sensitivity/<name>.rds (first knit only); summaries go to
# summary.rds and are rebuilt when missing, out of date, or older than main.rds.
# Uses from earlier chunks: d, here(), the model-code functions, FULL_FITS, MCMC, MAX_LAG,
#   TRAIN_END, PRIOR_TAU, post_dir, NAV, RED and the make-results helpers
#   (summ, param_mats, diag_group, kwh_curve, dow_full, seas_matrix, bf_sd).

OUT9    <- here("results", "09_sensitivity")
LOW_KWH <- 12      # absence-block threshold, as in Section 2
N_REP   <- 2000    # replicated series for the predictive checks

PRIORS <- list(
  coef_half   = list(prior_tau = c(10, 2.5)),
  coef_double = list(prior_tau = c(40, 10)),
  nu_heavy    = list(nu_exp_mean = 3),
  nu_light    = list(nu_exp_mean = 30,
                     mcmc = list(n_iter = 80000, burn = 20000, thin = 10, n_chains = 4))
)
HEADS <- c(main = "Reported", coef_half = "SDs halved", coef_double = "SDs doubled",
           nu_heavy = "$\\nu - 2$, mean 3", nu_light = "$\\nu - 2$, mean 30")

# ---------------- A. refit under one alternative prior ----------------
run_prior <- function(name, d) {
  pr  <- PRIORS[[name]]
  mc  <- if (is.null(pr$mcmc)) MCMC else pr$mcmc
  tau <- if (is.null(pr$prior_tau)) PRIOR_TAU$sqrt else pr$prior_tau
  f <- fit_chains(
    d$kwh, d$observed, d$t, d$dow,
    n_chains = mc$n_chains, seed = FULL_FITS$main$seed,
    J = 2, p = 1, heavy = TRUE, scale = "sqrt",
    n_iter = mc$n_iter, burn = mc$burn, thin = mc$thin,
    ll_index = common_ll_index(d$observed, max_lag = MAX_LAG),
    n_paths = 1, disperse_init = TRUE,
    prior_tau = tau,
    nu_exp_mean = if (is.null(pr$nu_exp_mean)) 10 else pr$nu_exp_mean
  )
  f$waic <- waic(f$loglik)
  f$conv <- diag_group(param_mats(f))
  f$prior_tau <- tau                                   # needed by bf_sd()
  f[c("loglik", "eps_path", "wt_path", "warmup", "eps_last")] <- NULL   # keep files small
  f
}

# the Section 5 conclusions, computed from one fit exactly as make_results() does
conclusions <- function(f) {
  b  <- flatten(f, "beta")
  nm <- f$names
  yr  <- seq(as.Date("2009-01-01"), as.Date("2009-12-31"), by = "day")
  win <- seq(as.Date("2009-07-01"), as.Date("2010-06-30"), by = "day")
  M2 <- kwh_curve(b, nm, yr, 2)
  add2 <- apply(abs(M2 - kwh_curve(b, nm, yr, 1)), 1, max)
  dl <- dow_full(b, nm)
  A  <- b[, match("intercept", nm)] + seas_matrix(b, nm, yr, 2)
  b_tr <- b[, match("trend_per_year", nm)]
  E <- rowMeans(A^2) + 2 * dl * rowMeans(A) + dl^2
  P <- E - rowMeans(E)
  wkend <- rowMeans(P[, 6:7]) - rowMeans(P[, 1:5])
  list(
    annual = summ(rowMeans(M2)),
    slope = summ(2 * b_tr * (rowMeans(A) + rowMeans(dl))),
    p_decline = mean(b_tr < 0),
    peak = summ(apply(kwh_curve(b, nm, win, 2), 1, max)),
    trough = summ(apply(M2, 1, min)),
    add2 = summ(add2), p_add2_gt1 = mean(add2 > 1),
    wkend = summ(wkend), p_wkend = mean(wkend > 0),
    phi = summ(as.numeric(f$phi)), sigma = summ(as.numeric(f$sigma)), nu = summ(as.numeric(f$nu))
  )
}

# ---------------- C. posterior predictive statistics (kWh, full calendar, NA = missing) ----------------
longest_run <- function(x) {
  r <- rle(!is.na(x) & x < LOW_KWH)
  if (any(r$values)) max(r$lengths[r$values]) else 0L
}
ppc_stats <- function(y, mon) {
  ok <- !is.na(y)
  v <- y[ok]
  pair <- ok[-1] & ok[-length(y)]
  winter <- ok & mon %in% c(12, 1, 2)
  summer <- ok & mon %in% c(6, 7, 8)
  c(lag1 = cor(y[-1][pair], y[-length(y)][pair]),
    sd_ratio = sd(y[winter]) / sd(y[summer]),
    skew = mean((v - mean(v))^3) / sd(v)^3,
    max = max(v),
    n_low = sum(v < LOW_KWH),
    run_low = longest_run(y))
}
PPC_LABELS <- c(
  lag1 = "Lag-1 autocorrelation of daily kWh",
  sd_ratio = "SD in Dec-Feb / SD in Jun-Aug",
  skew = "Skewness of daily kWh",
  max = "Highest day (kWh)",
  n_low = sprintf("Days below %d kWh", LOW_KWH),
  run_low = sprintf("Longest run of days below %d kWh", LOW_KWH)
)
replicate_series <- function(f, observed, n_rep, seed = 9) {
  # one posterior draw per series: systematic part plus an AR(1) error with t_nu(0, sigma)
  # innovations, started in its stationary state; simulated on the sqrt scale, squared back
  # to kWh, and blanked on the real missing days so both series are compared on the same days
  set.seed(seed)
  b <- flatten(f, "beta")
  sel <- sample.int(nrow(b), n_rep)
  sig <- as.numeric(f$sigma)[sel]; nu <- as.numeric(f$nu)[sel]; phi <- as.numeric(f$phi)[sel]
  mu <- b[sel, , drop = FALSE] %*% t(f$X)
  nT <- ncol(mu)
  eta <- matrix(rt(n_rep * nT, df = rep(nu, nT)), n_rep, nT) * sig   # t_nu(0, sigma) innovations
  eps <- matrix(0, n_rep, nT)
  eps[, 1] <- eta[, 1] / sqrt(1 - phi^2)
  for (i in 2:nT) eps[, i] <- phi * eps[, i - 1] + eta[, i]
  y_rep <- pmax(mu + eps, 0)^2
  y_rep[, !observed] <- NA
  y_rep
}

make_sensitivity <- function(d) {
  f0 <- readRDS(file.path(post_dir, "main.rds"))
  if (is.null(f0$prior_tau)) f0$prior_tau <- PRIOR_TAU$sqrt
  fits <- c(list(main = f0), lapply(setNames(names(PRIORS), names(PRIORS)),
                                    function(n) readRDS(file.path(OUT9, paste0(n, ".rds")))))
  for (n in names(fits)) if (length(fits[[n]]$waic$elpd_i) != length(f0$waic$elpd_i))
    stop("Fit '", n, "' uses different likelihood days from main. ",
         "Delete ", file.path(OUT9, paste0(n, ".rds")), " and knit again.")
  S9 <- list()

  # ---------------- A. prior sensitivity table ----------------
  res  <- lapply(fits, conclusions)
  conv <- t(vapply(names(PRIORS), function(n) fits[[n]]$conv, numeric(3)))
  d_elpd <- vapply(fits, function(f) {
    di <- f$waic$elpd_i - f0$waic$elpd_i
    c(diff = sum(di), se = sqrt(length(di) * var(di)))
  }, numeric(2))
  fmt <- function(s, dp = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f [%.", dp, "f, %.", dp, "f]"), s[1], s[2], s[3])
  col <- function(r, n) c(
    fmt(r$annual), fmt(r$slope, 2), sprintf("%.2f", r$p_decline), fmt(r$peak), fmt(r$trough),
    fmt(r$add2), fmt(r$wkend), fmt(r$phi, 2), fmt(r$nu),
    if (n == "main") "0 (reference)" else sprintf("%+.1f", round(d_elpd["diff", n], 1) + 0)   # + 0 turns -0 into 0
  )
  prior_tab <- data.frame(
    Quantity = c("Typical day, annual mean (kWh/day)", "Change in annual mean (kWh/day per year)",
                 "P(decline)", "Winter peak (kWh/day)", "Summer trough (kWh/day)",
                 "Largest change from second harmonic (kWh/day)", "Weekend minus weekday (kWh/day)",
                 "AR(1) coefficient $\\phi$", "Degrees of freedom $\\nu$", "Change in WAIC elpd"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  for (n in names(fits)) prior_tab[[HEADS[[n]]]] <- col(res[[n]], n)
  # largest shift of a kWh posterior mean, in posterior SDs (95% CrI width / 3.92)
  kwh_keys <- c("annual", "slope", "peak", "trough", "add2", "wkend")
  shift <- sapply(names(PRIORS), function(n) sapply(kwh_keys, function(k)
    abs(res[[n]][[k]][["mean"]] - res$main[[k]][["mean"]]) /
      ((res$main[[k]][["hi"]] - res$main[[k]][["lo"]]) / 3.92)))

  # ---------------- B. Savage-Dickey Bayes factors (log10 BF10, >0 favours the larger model) ----------------
  bf <- sapply(fits, function(f) c(trend = bf_sd(f, "trend_per_year"),
                                   harm2 = bf_sd(f, c("sin_h2", "cos_h2"))))
  bf_tab <- data.frame(
    Comparison = c("Linear trend: $\\beta_1 \\neq 0$ vs $\\beta_1 = 0$",
                   "Second harmonic: $J = 2$ vs $J = 1$"),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  for (n in names(fits)) bf_tab[[HEADS[[n]]]] <- sprintf("%+.2f", bf[, n])

  # ---------------- C. posterior predictive checks ----------------
  mon <- as.integer(format(d$date, "%m"))
  y_rep <- replicate_series(f0, d$observed, N_REP)
  obs_stat <- ppc_stats(d$kwh, mon)
  rep_stat <- t(apply(y_rep, 1, ppc_stats, mon = mon))
  ppp <- colMeans(rep_stat >= rep(obs_stat, each = N_REP))
  rq <- apply(rep_stat, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  dp <- c(lag1 = 2, sd_ratio = 2, skew = 2, max = 1, n_low = 0, run_low = 0)
  ppc_tab <- data.frame(
    Statistic = unname(PPC_LABELS[names(obs_stat)]),
    Observed = vapply(names(obs_stat), function(k) formatC(obs_stat[[k]], format = "f", digits = dp[[k]]), ""),
    `Replicated median [95% interval]` = vapply(names(obs_stat), function(k)
      sprintf(paste0("%.", dp[[k]], "f [%.", dp[[k]], "f, %.", dp[[k]], "f]"), rq[2, k], rq[1, k], rq[3, k]), ""),
    `P(replicated $\\geq$ observed)` = sprintf("%.3f", ppp),
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  # ---------------- D. held-out interval coverage by season ----------------
  ho <- readRDS(file.path(post_dir, "holdout.rds"))
  test <- d[d$date > TRAIN_END, ]
  r <- ho$roll[ho$roll$observed, ]
  r$date <- test$date[r$origin + r$h]
  m <- as.integer(format(r$date, "%m"))
  r$season <- factor(ifelse(m %in% c(12, 1, 2), "Winter (Dec-Feb)",
                     ifelse(m %in% 3:5, "Spring (Mar-May)",
                     ifelse(m %in% 6:8, "Summer (Jun-Aug)", "Autumn (Sep-Nov)"))),
                     levels = c("Winter (Dec-Feb)", "Spring (Mar-May)", "Summer (Jun-Aug)", "Autumn (Sep-Nov)"))
  rl <- rle(d$observed & d$kwh < LOW_KWH)
  ends <- cumsum(rl$lengths)
  absence <- rep(FALSE, nrow(d))
  for (i in which(rl$values & rl$lengths >= 5)) absence[(ends[i] - rl$lengths[i] + 1):ends[i]] <- TRUE
  r$absence <- absence[match(r$date, d$date)]
  cover <- function(x) c(n = nrow(x), c95 = mean(x$kwh >= x$lo95 & x$kwh <= x$hi95),
                         c50 = mean(x$kwh >= x$lo50 & x$kwh <= x$hi50), w95 = mean(x$hi95 - x$lo95))
  by_season    <- t(sapply(split(r, r$season), cover))
  by_season_ex <- t(sapply(split(r[!r$absence, ], r$season[!r$absence]), cover))
  season_tab <- data.frame(
    Season = rownames(by_season),
    `Forecasts scored` = sprintf("%.0f", by_season[, "n"]),
    `95% coverage` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * by_season[, "c95"]),
    `95% coverage, absence days removed` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * by_season_ex[, "c95"]),
    `50% coverage` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * by_season[, "c50"]),
    `Mean 95% width (kWh)` = sprintf("%.1f", by_season[, "w95"]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  S9 <- list(
    res = res, conv = conv, d_elpd = d_elpd, shift = shift, max_shift = max(shift), bf = bf,
    prior_tab = prior_tab, bf_tab = bf_tab, ppc_tab = ppc_tab, season_tab = season_tab,
    ppc = list(obs = obs_stat, rep_q = rq, ppp = ppp, n_rep = N_REP),
    fig11 = list(obs = obs_stat, rep_stat = rep_stat, ppp = ppp),
    season = by_season, season_ex = by_season_ex,
    absence_holdout_days = sum(absence[d$date > TRAIN_END])
  )
  saveRDS(S9, file.path(OUT9, "summary.rds"))
  invisible(S9)
}

# ---------------- run: refits only if missing, summaries only if missing or outdated ----------------
dir.create(OUT9, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
for (name in names(PRIORS)) {
  path <- file.path(OUT9, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) saveRDS(run_prior(name, d), path)
}
sum9 <- file.path(OUT9, "summary.rds")
needs9 <- !file.exists(sum9) || is.null(readRDS(sum9)$fig11) ||
  !all(names(PRIORS) %in% names(readRDS(sum9)$res)) ||               # a prior was added
  file.mtime(file.path(post_dir, "main.rds")) > file.mtime(sum9)     # main was refit after the summary
if (needs9) make_sensitivity(d)
S9 <- readRDS(sum9)
```

```{r sec6-numbers, include = FALSE}
# numbers quoted in Section 6 (fmt_n, fmt_ci and bf_word come from the sec5-numbers chunk)
pri <- names(PRIORS)
w <- S$waic; ao <- S$ar_order; pc <- S9$ppc
dash   <- function(x, dp = 1) paste(fmt_n(range(x), dp), collapse = "\u2013")
rng_to <- function(x) paste(fmt_n(range(x), 2), collapse = " to ")

# AR(4): do the Section 5 conclusions change? (conclusions() comes from the sensitivity chunk)
c4 <- conclusions(load_fit("ar4")); c1 <- S9$res$main
keys <- c("annual", "slope", "peak", "trough", "add2", "wkend")
shift4 <- max(sapply(keys, function(k) abs(c4[[k]][["mean"]] - c1[[k]][["mean"]]) /
                                         ((c1[[k]][["hi"]] - c1[[k]][["lo"]]) / 3.92)))
lpd   <- rbind(ao$ar2$roll_lpd, ao$ar4$roll_lpd)      # held-out log score change vs AR(1): diff, se
ar_ok <- all(lpd[, "diff"] < 2 * lpd[, "se"])         # TRUE = extra lags give no clear forecast gain

v6 <- list(
  max_shift = fmt_n(S9$max_shift, 2),
  p_dec  = paste(sprintf("%.2f", range(sapply(S9$res, `[[`, "p_decline"))), collapse = "\u2013"),
  d_elpd = fmt_n(max(abs(S9$d_elpd["diff", pri]))),
  nu_rng = dash(sapply(S9$res, function(r) r$nu[["mean"]])),
  n_ll = fmt_n(w$n, 0),
  J   = fmt_n(w$J2_vs_J1[["diff"]]),    J_se   = fmt_n(w$J2_vs_J1[["se"]]),
  kwh = fmt_n(w$sqrt_vs_kwh[["diff"]]), kwh_se = fmt_n(w$sqrt_vs_kwh[["se"]]),
  ar2 = fmt_n(w$ar2_vs_ar1[["diff"]]),  ar2_se = fmt_n(w$ar2_vs_ar1[["se"]]),
  ar4 = fmt_n(w$ar4_vs_ar1[["diff"]]),  ar4_se = fmt_n(w$ar4_vs_ar1[["se"]]),
  ar2_lpd = fmt_n(ao$ar2$roll_lpd[["diff"]], 3), ar2_lpd_se = fmt_n(ao$ar2$roll_lpd[["se"]], 3),
  ar4_lpd = fmt_n(ao$ar4$roll_lpd[["diff"]], 3), ar4_lpd_se = fmt_n(ao$ar4$roll_lpd[["se"]], 3),
  shift4 = fmt_n(shift4, 2),
  ar_end = if (ar_ok) "so we keep the simpler AR(1)" else
             "although AR(4) forecasts slightly better; we keep AR(1) because the conclusions do not change",
  bf_tr = fmt_n(S9$bf["trend", "main"], 2), bf_tr_rng = dash(S9$bf["trend", ], 2),
  bf_h2 = fmt_n(S9$bf["harm2", "main"], 2), bf_h2_rng = dash(S9$bf["harm2", ], 2),
  bf_tr2 = rng_to(S9$bf["trend", ]), bf_h22 = rng_to(S9$bf["harm2", ]),
  bf_tr_w = paste(unique(bf_word(range(S9$bf["trend", ]))), collapse = " to "),
  tr_dir = if (S9$bf["trend", "main"] < 0) "against" else "for",
  h2_dir = if (S9$bf["harm2", "main"] < 0) "against" else "for",
  n_rep = fmt_n(pc$n_rep, 0),
  p_sd  = sprintf("%.3f", pc$ppp[["sd_ratio"]]),
  run_obs = pc$obs[["run_low"]], run_lo = pc$rep_q[1, "run_low"], run_hi = pc$rep_q[3, "run_low"],
  run_p = if (pc$ppp[["run_low"]] == 0) "never reached" else
            sprintf("reached in only %.1f%%", 100 * pc$ppp[["run_low"]]),
  c95_rng = dash(100 * S9$season[, "c95"]),
  c50_rng = dash(100 * S9$season[, "c50"], 0),
  w_sum = fmt_n(S9$season["Summer (Jun-Aug)", "w95"]),
  w_win = fmt_n(S9$season["Winter (Dec-Feb)", "w95"]),
  conv_ok = all(S9$conv[, "rhat"] < 1.01 & S9$conv[, "ess"] > 400)
)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(S9$bf[, "main"]), c(bf_tr, bf_h2))))   # Section 5 and Table 11 agree
```

**Prior sensitivity.** We refit the final model four times, changing one prior at a time: the coefficient prior standard deviations halved (intercept 10, others 2.5 $\sqrt{\text{kWh}}$) or doubled (40 and 10), and the prior mean of $\nu - 2$ lowered from 10 to 3 (heavier tails) or raised to 30 (nearly Gaussian tails). No conclusion changes (Table 10). Every kWh summary moves by at most `r v6$max_shift` posterior standard deviations, $P(\text{decline})$ stays at `r v6$p_dec`, and WAIC's elpd changes by at most `r v6$d_elpd`. Even $\nu$ stays between `r v6$nu_rng` while its prior mean ranges from 5 to 32, so the evidence for heavy tails comes from the data.

**Bayes factors.(short version)** Because the coefficient priors are independent normals, the Bayes factors reported in Section 5 are Savage–Dickey density ratios: the prior density at zero divided by the posterior density at zero (Dickey, 1971; Verdinelli & Wasserman, 1995). Unlike posteriors, they depend on the prior width: doubling a coefficient's prior SD halves its prior density at zero, lowering $\log_{10}\text{BF}_{10}$ by about 0.3 per coefficient. Across the five priors, $\log_{10}\text{BF}_{10}$ ranges over `r v6$bf_tr_rng` for the trend and `r v6$bf_h2_rng` for the second harmonic (Table 11), so the direction and strength of the evidence do not depend on the prior.

**Bayes factors. (long version)** On the $\log_{10}$ scale, positive values favour the larger model, and $\pm 1$ and $\pm 2$ mark strong and decisive evidence (Kass & Raftery, 1995). Under the reported prior, $\log_{10} \text{BF}_{10}$ is `r v6$bf_tr` for the linear trend (`r v6$bf_tr_rng` across the five priors), evidence `r v6$tr_dir` including a trend, and `r v6$bf_h2` for the second harmonic (`r v6$bf_h2_rng`), evidence `r v6$h2_dir` $J = 2$ (Table 11). Bayes factors depend on the prior width in a way posteriors do not: doubling a coefficient's prior SD halves its prior density at zero, lowering $\log_{10}\text{BF}_{10}$ by about 0.3 per coefficient. Halving and doubling the SDs therefore brackets this effect, and the direction of the evidence is the same at every width.

**Modelling assumptions.** On the same `r v6$n_ll` likelihood terms, dropping the second harmonic lowers WAIC's elpd by `r v6$J` (SE `r v6$J_se`), and modelling raw kWh lowers it by `r v6$kwh` (SE `r v6$kwh_se`). AR(2) and AR(4) errors change it by `r v6$ar2` (SE `r v6$ar2_se`) and `r v6$ar4` (SE `r v6$ar4_se`), but on the held-out year their log score per forecast changes by `r v6$ar2_lpd` (SE `r v6$ar2_lpd_se`) and `r v6$ar4_lpd` (SE `r v6$ar4_lpd_se`) relative to AR(1), so we keep AR(1).

**Posterior predictive checks.** Across `r v6$n_rep` series simulated from the posterior, the model reproduces day-to-day persistence, skewness, the highest day and the number of low days (Table 12, Figure 11). The winter-to-summer spread ratio is borderline ($p =$ `r v6$p_sd`): the square-root scale removes most, not all, of the extra winter variability. The observed longest run below 12 kWh, `r v6$run_obs` days, is `r v6$run_p` of the replicates (95% interval `r v6$run_lo`–`r v6$run_hi` days), so the model cannot generate the absence blocks found under Q6.

**Calibration by season.** Held-out 95% intervals cover `r v6$c95_rng`% of days in every season, widening from `r v6$w_sum` kWh in summer to `r v6$w_win` kWh in winter, so the winter variability noted in Section 2.2 does not miscalibrate them (Table 13). The 50% intervals are less even (`r v6$c50_rng`%).

The answers to Q1–Q5 are robust to the priors and to these modelling choices; the only failure is the sustained absences already reported under Q6.

```{r fig11, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 6.5, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = sprintf("Figure 11. Posterior predictive checks. Histograms show each statistic over %s series simulated from the posterior (central 99%% shown); red lines mark the observed series.", v6$n_rep)}
local({
  p <- S9$fig11
  par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4.2, 4, 3, 1))
  for (k in names(p$obs)) {
    v  <- p$rep_stat[, k]
    xl <- range(c(quantile(v, c(0.005, 0.995)), p$obs[[k]]))
    v  <- v[v >= xl[1] & v <= xl[2]]                    # drop the most extreme replicates so bins are not stretched
    br <- if (k == "run_low") seq(floor(xl[1]) - 0.5, ceiling(xl[2]) + 0.5, by = 1) else
            seq(xl[1], xl[2], length.out = 40)
    hist(v, breaks = br, col = adjustcolor(NAV, 0.35), border = "white", xlim = xl,
         main = PPC_LABELS[[k]], xlab = sprintf("p = %.3f", p$ppp[[k]]), ylab = "replicated series",
         cex.main = 0.95)
    abline(v = p$obs[[k]], col = RED, lwd = 2.5)
  }
})
```

  caption = paste(
    sprintf("Table 13. Held-out predictive intervals by season, over the %d rolling origins and 1-60 day horizons of Section 5", S$fc$n_origins),
    sprintf("(fit through %s; missing days are not scored). 'Absence days removed' drops the %d absence-block days in the held-out year.",
            format(S$fc$train_end, "%d %B %Y"), S9$absence_holdout_days)
  )
)
```

# 7. Alternative Analysis, Comparison, and Bayesian Justification

```{r frequentist, include = FALSE}
# ---- Section 7: the frequentist alternative ----
# Fits the final model (sqrt kWh, trend, two harmonics, day of week, AR(1) errors with
# t_nu(0, sigma) innovations) by maximum likelihood, then repeats the Section 5 summaries and the
# holdout forecasts with the MLE. The likelihood is the same conditional likelihood as the Bayesian
# analysis: a day enters only if it and the previous day are observed, so the 23 missing days and
# the first day after each gap contribute no term (no imputation, no latent weights). The two
# analyses therefore differ only in priors versus maximum likelihood.
# Wald intervals use the observed information on the scale (beta, log sigma, atanh phi, log(nu - 2)),
# which keeps them inside the parameter space. kWh quantities are nonlinear in beta, so their
# intervals come from draws of the asymptotic normal distribution of the MLE (Krinsky and Robb,
# 1986), passed through the same functions used on the posterior draws.
# Results go to results/08_freq/summary.rds and are rebuilt when missing or out of date.
# Uses from earlier chunks: d, S, here(), post_dir, the model-code functions, TRAIN_END, ROLL_H,
# ROLL_STEP, MAX_LAG, NAV, RED and the make-results helpers (kwh_curve, dow_full, seas_matrix, q95).
OUT8  <- here("results", "08_freq")
N_SIM <- 20000L
GREEN <- "#148f77"

# ---------------- maximum likelihood ----------------
fit_mle <- function(kwh, observed, t, dow, J, t_center = mean(t)) {
  des <- build_design(t, dow, J, t_center = t_center)
  X <- des$X
  k <- ncol(X)
  z <- ifelse(observed, sqrt(kwh), NA_real_)            # model scale: sqrt(kWh)
  idx <- common_ll_index(observed, max_lag = 1)         # AR(1) likelihood needs the previous day
  Xd <- X[idx, , drop = FALSE]
  Xl <- X[idx - 1L, , drop = FALSE]
  zd <- z[idx]
  zl <- z[idx - 1L]

  unpack <- function(th) {
    list(beta = th[1:k], sigma = exp(th[k + 1]), phi = tanh(th[k + 2]), nu = 2 + exp(th[k + 3]))
  }
  parts <- function(th) {
    p <- unpack(th)
    el <- zl - as.numeric(Xl %*% p$beta)
    e <- (zd - as.numeric(Xd %*% p$beta)) - p$phi * el
    c(p, list(e = e, el = el))
  }
  nll <- function(th) {
    q <- parts(th)
    -sum(log_t(q$e, q$sigma, q$nu, TRUE))
  }
  grad <- function(th) {
    q <- parts(th)
    s2 <- q$sigma^2
    u <- q$e^2 / (q$nu * s2)
    w <- (q$nu + 1) / (q$nu + q$e^2 / s2)
    Xt <- Xd - q$phi * Xl
    d_beta <- colSums(Xt * (w * q$e / s2))
    d_phi <- sum(w * q$e * q$el / s2) * (1 - q$phi^2)
    d_lsig <- sum(-1 + w * q$e^2 / s2)
    d_nu <- sum(0.5 * digamma(0.5 * (q$nu + 1)) - 0.5 * digamma(0.5 * q$nu) - 0.5 / q$nu -
                  0.5 * log1p(u) + 0.5 * (q$nu + 1) * u / (q$nu * (1 + u)))
    -c(d_beta, d_lsig, d_phi, d_nu * (q$nu - 2))
  }

  ok <- observed
  b0 <- qr.solve(X[ok, , drop = FALSE], z[ok])
  th <- c(b0, log(sd(z[ok] - X[ok, ] %*% b0)), atanh(0.4), log(6))
  for (i in 1:3) {
    o <- optim(th, nll, grad, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 5000, reltol = 1e-15))
    th <- o$par
  }
  H <- optimHess(th, nll, grad)
  V <- solve(H)
  list(
    theta = th, V = V, se = sqrt(diag(V)), loglik = -o$value, n = length(idx),
    n_par = length(th), convergence = o$convergence, max_grad = max(abs(grad(th))),
    names = c(des$names, "log_sigma", "atanh_phi", "log_nu_minus_2"),
    beta_names = des$names, k = k, X = X, z = z, J = J, t_center = t_center, unpack = unpack,
    nll = nll, grad = grad
  )
}

# rows are draws of theta from N(theta_hat, V)
sim_theta <- function(m, n, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  Z <- matrix(rnorm(n * m$n_par), n, m$n_par)
  sweep(Z %*% chol(m$V), 2, m$theta, `+`)
}
wald <- function(m, name, f = identity) {
  i <- match(name, m$names)
  f(m$theta[i] + c(0, -1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * m$se[i])
}

# kWh quantities, per row of b (same definitions as make_results)
derived <- function(b, nm) {
  yr <- seq(as.Date("2009-01-01"), as.Date("2009-12-31"), by = "day")
  win <- seq(as.Date("2009-07-01"), as.Date("2010-06-30"), by = "day")
  M2 <- kwh_curve(b, nm, yr, 2)
  annual <- rowMeans(M2)
  peak <- apply(kwh_curve(b, nm, win, 2), 1, max)
  trough <- apply(M2, 1, min)
  add2 <- apply(abs(M2 - kwh_curve(b, nm, yr, 1)), 1, max)
  dl <- dow_full(b, nm)
  A <- b[, match("intercept", nm)] + seas_matrix(b, nm, yr, 2)
  slope <- 2 * b[, match("trend_per_year", nm)] * (rowMeans(A) + rowMeans(dl))
  E <- rowMeans(A^2) + 2 * dl * rowMeans(A) + dl^2
  P <- E - rowMeans(E)
  wkend <- rowMeans(P[, 6:7, drop = FALSE]) - rowMeans(P[, 1:5, drop = FALSE])
  cbind(annual = annual, slope_kwh = slope, slope_pct = 100 * slope / annual, peak_kwh = peak,
        trough_kwh = trough, swing = peak - trough, add2 = add2, wkend = wkend, thu = P[, 4])
}

# wrap parameter rows so that forecast() can use them
as_draws <- function(th, m, eps_last) {
  N <- nrow(th)
  k <- m$k
  list(
    beta = array(th[, 1:k], c(1, N, k)), sigma = matrix(exp(th[, k + 1]), 1),
    phi = array(tanh(th[, k + 2]), c(1, N, 1)), nu = matrix(2 + exp(th[, k + 3]), 1),
    eps_last = array(eps_last, c(1, N, 1)), p = 1L, J = m$J, heavy = TRUE, scale = "sqrt"
  )
}

# ---------------- holdout forecasts with the MLE ----------------
freq_holdout <- function(d, n_single = 4000L, n_roll = 1500L) {
  train <- d[d$date <= TRAIN_END, ]
  test <- d[d$date > TRAIN_END, ]
  rownames(test) <- NULL
  t_center <- mean(train$t)
  m <- fit_mle(train$kwh, train$observed, train$t, train$dow, J = 2, t_center = t_center)
  last <- nrow(train)
  stopifnot(train$observed[last])
  Xtest <- build_design(test$t, test$dow, 2, t_center = t_center)$X
  z_test <- sqrt(test$kwh)

  # plug-in: every path uses the MLE; est_err: each path first draws theta from N(theta_hat, V)
  sets <- list(
    plugin = function(n) matrix(m$theta, n, m$n_par, byrow = TRUE),
    est_err = function(n) sim_theta(m, n, seed = 81)
  )
  out <- list(train_phi = m$unpack(m$theta)$phi, n_train = sum(train$observed))
  for (nm in names(sets)) {
    th <- sets[[nm]](n_single)
    eps_last <- m$z[last] - as.numeric(th[, 1:m$k] %*% m$X[last, ])
    fc <- forecast(as_draws(th, m, eps_last), test$t, test$dow, t_center, seed = 99)
    q <- apply(fc$y, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))
    sg <- data.frame(kwh = test$kwh, lo95 = q[1, ], lo50 = q[2, ], med = q[3, ], hi50 = q[4, ],
                     hi95 = q[5, ], crps = crps(fc$y, test$kwh))[test$observed, ]
    single <- c(c95 = mean(sg$kwh >= sg$lo95 & sg$kwh <= sg$hi95),
                c50 = mean(sg$kwh >= sg$lo50 & sg$kwh <= sg$hi50),
                crps = mean(sg$crps), mae = mean(abs(sg$kwh - sg$med)), w95 = mean(sg$hi95 - sg$lo95))

    # rolling origins: the same rule as run_holdout() in the fit-models chunk, so the days match
    th <- sets[[nm]](n_roll)
    eps_test <- matrix(z_test, n_roll, length(z_test), byrow = TRUE) - th[, 1:m$k] %*% t(Xtest)
    origins <- seq(MAX_LAG, nrow(test) - 1L, by = ROLL_STEP)
    origins <- origins[vapply(origins, function(o) all(test$observed[(o - MAX_LAG + 1L):o]), logical(1))]
    rows <- vector("list", length(origins))
    for (oi in seq_along(origins)) {
      o <- origins[oi]
      idx <- (o + 1L):min(o + ROLL_H, nrow(test))
      fcr <- forecast(as_draws(th, m, eps_test[, o]), test$t[idx], test$dow[idx], t_center,
                      eps_init = eps_test[, o, drop = FALSE], seed = 7L * oi)
      qq <- apply(fcr$y, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.75, 0.975))
      rows[[oi]] <- data.frame(
        origin = o, h = seq_along(idx), observed = test$observed[idx], kwh = test$kwh[idx],
        lo95 = qq[1, ], lo50 = qq[2, ], hi50 = qq[3, ], hi95 = qq[4, ], crps = crps(fcr$y, test$kwh[idx])
      )
    }
    r <- do.call(rbind, rows)
    r <- r[r$observed, ]
    r$w95 <- r$hi95 - r$lo95
    r$c95 <- r$kwh >= r$lo95 & r$kwh <= r$hi95
    r$c50 <- r$kwh >= r$lo50 & r$kwh <= r$hi50
    out[[nm]] <- list(single = single, byh = aggregate(cbind(w95, c95, c50, crps) ~ h, data = r, FUN = mean),
                      n_origins = length(origins))
  }
  out
}

make_freq <- function(d) {
  dir.create(OUT8, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  out <- list()

  # ---------------- full-data fits: J = 2 (final) and J = 1 ----------------
  m2 <- fit_mle(d$kwh, d$observed, d$t, d$dow, J = 2)
  m1 <- fit_mle(d$kwh, d$observed, d$t, d$dow, J = 1)
  stopifnot(m2$convergence == 0, m1$convergence == 0, m2$n == m1$n)
  lr <- 2 * (m2$loglik - m1$loglik)
  out$fit <- list(
    n_terms = m2$n, loglik = c(J2 = m2$loglik, J1 = m1$loglik), max_grad = m2$max_grad,
    theta = setNames(m2$theta, m2$names), se = setNames(m2$se, m2$names),
    lrt_J2_vs_J1 = c(stat = lr, df = 2, p = pchisq(lr, 2, lower.tail = FALSE)),
    aic = c(J2 = 2 * m2$n_par - 2 * m2$loglik, J1 = 2 * m1$n_par - 2 * m1$loglik)
  )

  # ---------------- parameters and kWh quantities ----------------
  b_hat <- matrix(m2$theta[1:m2$k], 1, dimnames = list(NULL, m2$beta_names))
  point <- derived(b_hat, m2$beta_names)[1, ]
  th <- sim_theta(m2, N_SIM, seed = 8)
  sims <- derived(th[, 1:m2$k, drop = FALSE], m2$beta_names)
  ci <- apply(sims, 2, q95)
  est <- lapply(colnames(sims), function(q) c(est = point[[q]], lo = ci[1, q], hi = ci[2, q]))
  names(est) <- colnames(sims)
  est$phi <- wald(m2, "atanh_phi", tanh)
  est$sigma <- wald(m2, "log_sigma", exp)
  est$nu <- wald(m2, "log_nu_minus_2", function(x) 2 + exp(x))
  zt <- m2$theta[match("trend_per_year", m2$names)] / m2$se[match("trend_per_year", m2$names)]
  out$est <- est
  # one-sided p is for H0: beta1 >= 0 against a decline
  out$trend_test <- c(z = zt, p_two_sided = 2 * pnorm(-abs(zt)), p_one_sided = pnorm(zt))
  out$sim_vs_wald_beta_sd <- max(abs(apply(th[, 1:m2$k], 2, sd) / m2$se[1:m2$k] - 1))

  # how closely the two analyses agree on the typical-day quantities
  keys <- c("annual", "slope_kwh", "peak_kwh", "trough_kwh", "swing", "add2", "wkend")
  out$agree <- list(
    max_diff = max(sapply(keys, function(q) abs(est[[q]][1] - S$post[[q]][1]))),
    max_width_rel = max(sapply(keys, function(q) abs(diff(est[[q]][2:3]) / diff(S$post[[q]][2:3]) - 1)))
  )

  # ---------------- holdout forecasts ----------------
  out$holdout <- freq_holdout(d)
  stopifnot(out$holdout$plugin$n_origins == S$fc$n_origins)   # same forecast days as Section 5

  # ---------------- comparison table ----------------
  bp <- S$post
  bfc <- S$fc
  f1 <- function(s, dp = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f [%.", dp, "f, %.", dp, "f]"), s[1], s[2], s[3])
  pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
  hp <- out$holdout$plugin
  roll_cov <- function(b) paste(pct(mean(b$c95)), "/", pct(mean(b$c50)))
  widths <- function(b) sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", b$w95[1], mean(b$w95[b$h >= 3]))
  tab <- data.frame(
    Quantity = c(
      "Typical-day consumption, annual mean (kWh/day)",
      "Change in annual mean (kWh/day per year)",
      "Evidence about the trend",
      "Winter peak (kWh/day)",
      "Summer trough (kWh/day)",
      "Largest change from adding the second harmonic (kWh/day)",
      "Second harmonic: model comparison",
      "Weekend minus weekday (kWh/day)",
      "AR(1) coefficient $\\phi$",
      "Degrees of freedom $\\nu$",
      "Innovation scale $\\sigma$ ($\\sqrt{\\text{kWh}}$)",
      "Rolling forecasts, 1-60 days ahead: 95% / 50% interval coverage",
      "12-month forecast: mean absolute error (kWh/day)",
      "Mean 95% interval width, 1 day / 3-60 days ahead (kWh)"
    ),
    Bayesian = c(
      f1(bp$annual), f1(bp$slope_kwh, 2),
      sprintf("$P(\\text{decline} \\mid \\text{data}) = %.2f$", bp$p_decline),
      f1(bp$peak_kwh), f1(bp$trough_kwh), f1(bp$add2),
      sprintf("WAIC gain %.1f (SE %.1f)", S$waic$J2_vs_J1[["diff"]], S$waic$J2_vs_J1[["se"]]),
      f1(bp$wkend), f1(bp$phi, 2), f1(bp$nu), f1(bp$sigma, 2),
      roll_cov(bfc$byh), sprintf("%.1f", bfc$single[["mae"]]), widths(bfc$byh)
    ),
    Frequentist = c(
      f1(est$annual), f1(est$slope_kwh, 2),
      sprintf("$p = %.2f$ two-sided, $%.2f$ one-sided (decline)",
              out$trend_test[["p_two_sided"]], out$trend_test[["p_one_sided"]]),
      f1(est$peak_kwh), f1(est$trough_kwh), f1(est$add2),
      sprintf("LRT $\\chi^2_2 = %.1f$, $p %s$; AIC lower by %.1f", lr,
              if (out$fit$lrt_J2_vs_J1[["p"]] < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.3f", out$fit$lrt_J2_vs_J1[["p"]]),
              out$fit$aic[["J1"]] - out$fit$aic[["J2"]]),
      f1(est$wkend), f1(est$phi, 2), f1(est$nu), f1(est$sigma, 2),
      roll_cov(hp$byh), sprintf("%.1f", hp$single[["mae"]]), widths(hp$byh)
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  names(tab)[2:3] <- c("Bayesian: posterior mean [95% CrI]", "Frequentist: MLE [95% CI]")
  out$table <- tab

  saveRDS(out, file.path(OUT8, "summary.rds"))
  invisible(out)
}

sum8 <- file.path(OUT8, "summary.rds")
needs8 <- !file.exists(sum8) || is.null(readRDS(sum8)$agree) ||
  readRDS(sum8)$holdout$plugin$n_origins != S$fc$n_origins ||
  file.mtime(file.path(post_dir, "summary.rds")) > file.mtime(sum8)   # Bayesian results were rebuilt
if (needs8) make_freq(d)
F7 <- readRDS(sum8)
```

```{r sec7-numbers, include = FALSE}
# numbers quoted in Section 7 (fmt_n comes from the sec5-numbers chunk)
hp <- F7$holdout$plugin$byh; he <- F7$holdout$est_err$byh; hb <- S$fc$byh
w3 <- function(b) mean(b$w95[b$h >= 3])
v7 <- list(
  n_terms = fmt_n(F7$fit$n_terms, 0),
  n_orig = F7$holdout$plugin$n_origins,
  max_diff = fmt_n(F7$agree$max_diff),
  max_w = fmt_n(ceiling(100 * F7$agree$max_width_rel), 0),
  nu_f = fmt_n(F7$est$nu[1]), nu_b = fmt_n(S$post$nu[1]),
  p2 = sprintf("%.2f", F7$trend_test[["p_two_sided"]]),
  p_dec = sprintf("%.2f", S$post$p_decline),
  one_minus_p1 = sprintf("%.2f", 1 - F7$trend_test[["p_one_sided"]]),
  lrt = fmt_n(F7$fit$lrt_J2_vs_J1[["stat"]]),
  lrt_p = if (F7$fit$lrt_J2_vs_J1[["p"]] < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", F7$fit$lrt_J2_vs_J1[["p"]]),
  aic = fmt_n(F7$fit$aic[["J1"]] - F7$fit$aic[["J2"]]),
  waic = fmt_n(S$waic$J2_vs_J1[["diff"]]), waic_dev = fmt_n(2 * S$waic$J2_vs_J1[["diff"]]),
  narrow1 = fmt_n(100 * (1 - hp$w95[1] / hb$w95[1])),
  narrow3 = fmt_n(100 * (1 - w3(hp) / w3(hb))),
  c95_f = fmt_n(100 * mean(hp$c95)), c95_b = fmt_n(100 * mean(hb$c95)),
  mae_f = fmt_n(F7$holdout$plugin$single[["mae"]]), mae_b = fmt_n(S$fc$single[["mae"]]),
  gap_closed = {
  gap <- w3(hb) - w3(hp)   # how much narrower the plug-in intervals are
  if (gap > 0.1) fmt_n(100 * (w3(he) - w3(hp)) / gap, 0) else "n/a"
  }
)
```

**Frequentist analysis.** We refit the final model (the same $\sqrt{\text{kWh}}$ mean structure and AR(1) $t$ errors) by maximum likelihood, with no priors. The likelihood conditions on the first day of each observed run, so the 23 missing days drop out rather than being imputed, leaving `r v7$n_terms` terms. Standard errors come from the observed information. Typical-day kWh quantities are nonlinear in $\beta$, so their confidence intervals come from simulating the estimator's asymptotic normal distribution (Krinsky and Robb, 1986). Forecasts plug the training-period estimates into the AR(1) recursion and are scored on the same `r v7$n_orig` rolling origins as Section 5.

**Estimates and uncertainty.** Every typical-day estimate agrees with its posterior mean to within `r v7$max_diff` kWh, and their interval widths differ by under `r v7$max_w`% (Table 14, Figure 10a). With `r v7$n_terms` likelihood terms, the weakly informative priors carry almost no weight. The largest difference is the tail weight, $\hat\nu =$ `r v7$nu_f` against a posterior mean of `r v7$nu_b`, because the posterior of $\nu$ is right-skewed and its prior mean is 12.

**Interpretation.** The conclusions match; only the wording differs. For the trend, the frequentist analysis cannot reject zero ($p =$ `r v7$p2`), while the Bayesian analysis gives a decline probability of `r v7$p_dec`. That is close to one minus the one-sided $p$-value (`r v7$one_minus_p1`), as expected under weak priors, but only the Bayesian number is a probability about this household's trend. Both keep the second harmonic: the likelihood-ratio test gives $\chi^2_2 =$ `r v7$lrt` (`r v7$lrt_p`), and AIC improves by `r v7$aic`, close to the WAIC gain of `r v7$waic` expressed on the same deviance scale (`r v7$waic_dev`).

**Predictions.** Plug-in intervals treat the estimates as known, so they are `r v7$narrow1`% narrower one day ahead and `r v7$narrow3`% narrower from day three onward (Figure 10b). Their 95% coverage is `r v7$c95_f`%, against `r v7$c95_b`% (Figure 10c), and the 12-month forecasts miss by `r v7$mae_f` and `r v7$mae_b` kWh per day on average. Drawing the parameters from the estimator's sampling distribution closes about `r v7$gap_closed`% of the width gap, so parameter uncertainty is a small part of forecast uncertainty here.

**Why Bayesian?** For this household, the Bayesian analysis adds little to the estimates or forecasts: four years of daily data give both methods the same answers to all six questions. Its advantages are interpretation and bookkeeping. Every kWh summary, including peak dates and the 14-day anomaly check, comes from transforming posterior draws, with no delta method or asymptotic approximation. Parameter uncertainty, the 23 missing days and the latent $t$ weights all reach the forecasts without extra steps. A question like "how likely is a decline?" gets a direct answer. The cost is several minutes of MCMC and convergence checking per model, against seconds of optimization. With less data, such as a newly metered household, the priors and full predictive distribution would matter more.

local({
  bp <- S$post; bfc <- S$fc; est <- F7$est

  plot(NA, xlim = range(c(bb, ff)), ylim = c(0.5, length(keys) + 0.5), yaxt = "n", ylab = "",
       xlab = "kWh/day", main = "(a) Estimates with 95% intervals", las = 1)
  axis(2, at = yy, labels = labs, las = 1, cex.axis = 0.9)
  segments(bb[, 2], yy + 0.12, bb[, 3], yy + 0.12, col = NAV, lwd = 2)

  points(ff[, 1], yy - 0.12, pch = 17, col = RED)
  legend("bottomright", legend = c("Bayesian (posterior mean, CrI)", "Frequentist (MLE, CI)"),
         col = c(NAV, RED), pch = c(16, 17), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
  par(mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
  plot(bfc$byh$h, bfc$byh$w95, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = NAV,
       ylim = c(0, 1.1 * max(bfc$byh$w95, hp$byh$w95, he$byh$w95)),
       xlab = "forecast horizon (days ahead)", ylab = "mean width of 95% interval (kWh)",
       main = "(b) Predictive uncertainty by horizon", las = 1)
  lines(hp$byh$h, hp$byh$w95, lwd = 2, col = RED, lty = 2)
  lines(he$byh$h, he$byh$w95, lwd = 1.5, col = GREEN, lty = 3)
  legend("bottomright", legend = c("Bayesian predictive", "frequentist plug-in", "plug-in + estimation error"),
         col = c(NAV, RED, GREEN), lty = c(1, 2, 3), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
  bins <- cut(bfc$byh$h, c(0, 1, 7, 14, 30, 60), labels = c("1", "2-7", "8-14", "15-30", "31-60"))
  cov_bin <- function(b, key) 100 * tapply(b[[key]], bins, mean)
  xb <- seq_along(levels(bins))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0.5, length(xb) + 0.5), ylim = c(35, 100), xaxt = "n", las = 1,
       xlab = "forecast horizon (days ahead)", ylab = "empirical coverage (%)",
       main = "(c) Calibration by horizon")
  axis(1, at = xb, labels = levels(bins))
  abline(h = c(95, 50), lty = 3)
  points(xb - 0.1, cov_bin(bfc$byh, "c95"), pch = 16, col = NAV)
  points(xb + 0.1, cov_bin(hp$byh, "c95"), pch = 17, col = RED)
  points(xb - 0.1, cov_bin(bfc$byh, "c50"), pch = 1, col = NAV)
  points(xb + 0.1, cov_bin(hp$byh, "c50"), pch = 2, col = RED)
  text(length(xb) + 0.45, c(95, 50), c("95%", "50%"), pos = 3, cex = 0.8)
  legend("right", legend = c("Bayesian predictive", "frequentist plug-in", "filled: 95% interval",
                             "open: 50% interval"),
         col = c(NAV, RED, "grey30", "grey30"), pch = c(16, 17, 16, 1), bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
})
```
# 8. Innovation or Extension (needs to sound more human)

**Motivation.** A routine Bayesian regression assumes normal errors. Our EDA showed heavier tails than a normal on the square-root scale (Figure 3c): isolated days lie far above or below the typical day. Under normal errors, each such day pulls the fitted seasonal curve toward it and inflates $\sigma$, widening every credible and predictive interval.

**What we changed.** We replaced the normal innovations with Student-$t$ innovations, $\eta_t \sim t_\nu(0, \sigma)$, and treated the tail weight $\nu$ as unknown, with $\nu - 2 \sim \text{Exponential}(\text{mean } 10)$ so the variance stays finite. Because the $t$ likelihood is not conjugate to the normal priors, we wrote our own block random-walk Metropolis sampler on $(\beta, \log\sigma, \phi, \log(\nu - 2))$, combined with AR(1) errors and a conditional likelihood that leaves the 23 missing days out.

**What we learned.** The data favour heavy tails: $\nu =$ `r v$nu`, far from the normal limit $\nu \to \infty$, and between `r v6$nu_rng` under priors whose mean ranges from 5 to 32 (Table 10). Under the $t$ likelihood, `r v$n_lowW` isolated extreme days receive less than half the weight of a typical day, so they barely move the seasonal and weekly estimates. The extension also showed its limit: heavy tails absorb single unusual days but not sustained absences, and the posterior predictive check never reproduces the observed `r v6$run_obs`-day low run (Table 12). That points to a different next step: a hidden "away" state, such as a two-regime or hidden Markov model, rather than heavier tails.
